## Phase SK.00.LoggingStandardEnforcement — Governance: Architecture Enforcement for the Platform Logging Standard

### Goal

WO-041 (P-249/P-250) introduced the root `CLAUDE.md`'s new "Logging Conventions" section mandating `[LoggerMessage]`-only log authoring with explicit, per-domain-ranged `EventId`s — motivated by a live audit finding three incompatible logging-authoring styles ([LoggerMessage] attribute, hand-written `LoggerMessage.Define`, direct `ILogger` extension-method calls) coexisting with zero mechanical enforcement, plus two confirmed live `EventId` collisions (`SharedKernel.Caching.Redis.Core` vs `Redis.PubSub` both using 4001/4002; three internal collisions inside `SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit`). This domain's own established precedent — the reflection ban (SK0012), the raw-`HttpClient` ban (SK0013), the `ProblemDetails`/inline-`Result` bans (`PresentationLayeringRules`), and the marker-interface misuse bans (SK0017–19) — is that a platform-wide "always X, never Y" rule documented in prose alone will drift under multi-team, multi-package growth unless backed by a build-time gate. This phase ships that gate: two Roslyn diagnostics (SK0020, SK0021) banning the two hand-rolled authoring styles, plus a new architecture-test helper (`LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`) mechanically enforcing global `EventId` uniqueness and per-domain range membership against the `01.Core` registry (P-249).

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (one new analyzer class, two new diagnostics: SK0020, SK0021); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (one new public helper class: `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Analyzers/LoggingAuthoringStyleAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test files in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion.cs`
  - Corresponding test files in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0020 | DirectILoggerExtensionMethodUsage | Design | Warning | A call resolves (semantic model) to `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerExtensions.Log*` or `ILogger.Log` directly |
| SK0021 | HandWrittenLoggerMessageDefineDelegate | Design | Warning | A call's qualifier/name shape is `LoggerMessage.Define*` (syntax-only) |

### Implementation Rules

1. Both diagnostics are implemented in a SINGLE `DiagnosticAnalyzer` class, `LoggingAuthoringStyleAnalyzer` — the first two-diagnostics-one-class shape in this domain (every prior SK analyzer was one class per ID). Justified because both rules encode the same platform standard ("always `[LoggerMessage]`, never hand-rolled") and share two guards: the `SharedKernel.Testing` namespace exemption and the `GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.None` generated-code guard.
2. SK0020 requires `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` on the invoked method, checking `ContainingType` for an EXACT match against `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerExtensions` (`Name` starting with `"Log"`) or `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger` (`Name == "Log"`). A syntax-only simple-name check was rejected — `LogInformation`/`LogWarning`/etc. collide with unrelated logging frameworks (Serilog's own `ILogger`, NLog, custom wrapper types) that may coexist in a consuming microservice's dependency tree, and a false positive here would be maximally disruptive (this diagnostic is expected to fire, correctly, across nearly every production assembly platform-wide once wired into CI).
3. SK0021 is syntax-only: `InvocationExpressionSyntax` whose `Expression` is a `MemberAccessExpressionSyntax` with an `Expression` identifier text of `"LoggerMessage"` and a `Name` identifier text starting with `"Define"` (covers `Define`/`DefineScope` across all generic arities). No semantic model — the qualified `LoggerMessage.Define*` shape is specific enough that the cost of a symbol resolution is not justified, consistent with this domain's established "escalate only when truly ambiguous" discipline.
4. `LoggingAuthoringStyleAnalyzer` MUST call `context.ConfigureGeneratedCodeAnalysis(GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.None)` before registering any syntax-node action. This is load-bearing: `[LoggerMessage]`'s own source generator emits a partial-method body that internally calls `ILogger.Log` directly — without this guard, SK0020 would fire against the generated implementation of every correctly-authored `[LoggerMessage]` method platform-wide, which would be a self-defeating false positive at the core of this rule's entire purpose. Verify this specifically with a test fixture: a real `[LoggerMessage]`-attributed partial method declaration must NOT trigger SK0020, even though its generated body calls `ILogger.Log`.
5. Both diagnostics carry a `SharedKernel.Testing` namespace exemption (SyntaxNode.Parent walk, the established SK0001/SK0007 pattern) — the in-memory `ILogger`/`ILoggerFactory` test double (P-258, `16.Testing`) legitimately implements/exercises the `ILogger` surface directly as its own subject under test.
6. `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion` is a plain public helper class, NOT a `ConditionList`/`ICustomRule` — mirroring `ApplicationPipelineRules.PipelineOrderAssertion`'s precedent (a cross-cutting, whole-platform invariant with no single-assembly "fire on a contrived violating assembly" shape). It accepts `IReadOnlyDictionary<Assembly, (int RangeMin, int RangeMax)> assemblyRanges` — supplied entirely by the caller, since `00.Governance` never references `SharedKernel.Primitives` (it references nothing in production code). The consuming test project builds this dictionary from `SharedKernel.Primitives.Logging.LoggingEventIdRanges` (P-249) constants.
7. `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion` walks Mono.Cecil `ModuleDefinition.Types` PLUS `TypeDefinition.NestedTypes` RECURSIVELY by hand — it deliberately does NOT use `NetArchTest.Types.InAssembly(...)`, because SK0012's own documented gap (see `ReflectionGuardRules` in `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`) proved that projection never surfaces compiler-generated or nested types to an `ICustomRule`. This sidesteps that exact blind spot so a `[LoggerMessage]` method declared inside a nested logging-helper class is never missed.
8. For each `[LoggerMessage]`-attributed `MethodDefinition` found, extract `EventId` via the attribute's `EventId` named property (`CustomAttribute.Properties`) if present, falling back to the first `int`-typed positional `CustomAttribute.ConstructorArguments` entry — covering both `[LoggerMessage(EventId = N, ...)]` and `[LoggerMessage(N, LogLevel.X, "...")]` authoring styles. Verify the exact `LoggerMessageAttribute` constructor overload set and property names empirically via direct Mono.Cecil inspection of the .NET 10 `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` reference assembly (mirroring the confirmed-declaring-type-names verification already performed for `HealthCheckConstantsUsageRules`, WO-028 P-178) before finalizing the extraction logic.
9. Aggregate ALL violations (both collisions and out-of-range entries) across the ENTIRE supplied assembly set before throwing — do not stop at the first failure. Throw a single test-framework-agnostic assertion exception listing every offending site, mirroring `PipelineOrderAssertion`'s aggregate-failure-message convention.
10. This rule is EXPECTED TO FAIL if pointed at the platform's real shipped assemblies today — none of the ten WO-041 domain retrofit phases have shipped (all `○` Pending per root `CLAUDE.md` as of 2026-07-08), including `01.Core`'s own P-249 `LoggingEventIdRanges` registry. Design, implementation, and tests for this phase use CONTRIVED in-memory multi-assembly Mono.Cecil fixtures only (built via `CSharpCompilation` + `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage`, the established technique from `RedisTopologyRulesTests`/`CompositionRootExclusivityRules` fixtures). Do not attempt a real-assembly wiring pass in this phase.
11. SK0020 and SK0021 are the next two sequential IDs in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0019 was the prior ID). Both target `netstandard2.0` and pin `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 4.14.0`, matching every prior SK analyzer. Zero new NuGet dependency for either the analyzer or the architecture-test helper (`Mono.Cecil >= 0.11.5` already referenced in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` covers `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`).

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `Analyzers/LoggingAuthoringStyleAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0020 + SK0021 — bans direct `ILogger` extension-method calls and hand-written `LoggerMessage.Define` delegates |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/LoggingAuthoringStyleAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire-path + pass-path tests for both diagnostics, including a `[LoggerMessage]`-generated-code non-firing case and a `SharedKernel.Testing`-namespaced non-firing case |
| `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | Cross-assembly `EventId` global-uniqueness + per-domain-range-membership assertion helper |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertionTests.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Create | Contrived multi-assembly fixtures: collision fire path, out-of-range fire path, clean pass path (including a nested-type-declared `[LoggerMessage]` method proving the recursive walk) |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | Diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] SK0020 fires on `logger.LogInformation(...)`, `logger.LogWarning(...)`, `logger.LogError(...)`, and `logger.Log(LogLevel.X, ...)` call sites resolved (via semantic model) to `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerExtensions`/`ILogger`, and does NOT fire on a call to an unrelated type's same-named method, nor on the compiler-generated body of a `[LoggerMessage]`-attributed partial method, nor inside `SharedKernel.Testing`
- [ ] SK0021 fires on `LoggerMessage.Define<T1>(...)`/`LoggerMessage.DefineScope(...)` call sites assigned to a hand-written static delegate field, and does NOT fire on ordinary `[LoggerMessage]` attribute usage (no manual `Define` call present) nor inside `SharedKernel.Testing`
- [ ] `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion.AssertGloballyUniqueAndInRange` throws an aggregate exception naming both offending sites when two contrived fixture assemblies declare `[LoggerMessage]` methods sharing the same `EventId`
- [ ] `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion.AssertGloballyUniqueAndInRange` throws naming the offending type/method/actual-EventId/expected-range when a contrived fixture assembly declares an `EventId` outside its supplied range
- [ ] `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion.AssertGloballyUniqueAndInRange` does not throw when every contrived fixture `EventId` is globally unique and within its own assembly's supplied range — including one declared inside a nested type, proving the recursive `TypeDefinition.NestedTypes` walk actually reaches it
- [ ] Both SK IDs (SK0020, SK0021) and `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion` are recorded in `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`'s diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, and implementation rules with the same structure as every prior SK entry
- [ ] Full `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests` and `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` suites remain green after the new tests land (baseline: 115/115 analyzer tests and 130/130 architecture tests as of `SK.00.MarkerInterfaceMisuseGuard`/`SK.00.DomainEventDispatcherReflectionExemption` closeout)

### Dependencies

- Depends on `01.Core` P-249 (`SharedKernel.Primitives.Logging.LoggingEventIdRanges`) for the EVENTUAL real-assembly range dictionary only — NOT required for this phase's own design, implementation, or tests, which supply their own literal `(RangeMin, RangeMax)` tuples for contrived fixture assemblies. P-249 is itself `○` Pending as of this phase's authoring (2026-07-08); this phase's own SK0020/SK0021/`LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion` deliverables are not blocked by that fact.
- Unblocks: gives WO-041's "Logging Conventions" root `CLAUDE.md` section a mechanical enforcement mechanism, mirroring the precedent set for the raw-`HttpClient` ban (P-159), the `ProblemDetails`/inline-`Result` bans (P-199), and the marker-interface misuse bans (P-248) — without this phase, WO-041's platform-wide logging standard would remain "documented now, enforced never," the exact failure mode this domain's own precedent warns against.

### Tooling Version Notes

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp`: 4.14.0 (existing pin — SK0020/SK0021 reuse it, no version change)
- `Mono.Cecil`: >= 0.11.5 (existing pin — `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion` reuses it, no version change)
- Target framework: `netstandard2.0` (`SharedKernel.Analyzers`) / `net10.0` (`SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`)

### SK.00.LoggingStandardEnforcement — Task Rows

<!-- phase-key: SK.00.MagicStringGuard -->
## Phase SK.00.MagicStringGuard — Governance: Roslyn Analyzer + Architecture Test for Magic-String Prohibition

### Goal

WO-042 (P-264) closes the class of incident P-261 exemplified — `01.Core`'s new `WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys` (P-259 design) exist as documented constants, but nothing stops a second, independently-typed literal (e.g. `"CorrelationId"` vs `"correlation.id"`) from being hand-rolled at a call site that should have referenced them, or from being redeclared under a different name in a second package. This phase mirrors the established precedent — raw `HttpClient` (SK0013/P-159), inline `ProblemDetails` (`PresentationLayeringRules`/P-199), ad hoc logging (SK0020/SK0021/P-250) — by shipping a Roslyn diagnostic (SK0022) that flags a raw string literal at any of four recognized cross-cutting call-site shapes (HTTP header indexer/setter, `Activity.SetBaggage`/`.SetTag`, `IConfiguration.GetSection`, `ClaimsPrincipal`/`Claim` comparison), plus a companion architecture-test helper confirming `01.Core`'s `WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys` are the sole declared literal for their own values platform-wide.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (one new analyzer class, one new diagnostic: SK0022); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (one new public helper class: `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion`)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Analyzers/CrossCuttingMagicStringLiteralAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test files in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion.cs`
  - Corresponding test files in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0022 | CrossCuttingMagicStringLiteral | Usage | Warning | A raw string-literal token (`LiteralExpressionSyntax` of kind `StringLiteralExpression`) supplied at one of four recognized call-site shapes: `HttpHeaders`/`IHeaderDictionary` indexer or `.Add`/`.TryAddWithoutValidation`; `Activity.SetBaggage`/`.SetTag`; `IConfiguration.GetSection`; `ClaimsPrincipal`/`Claim` comparison against a claim-type string |

### Implementation Rules

1. SK0022 is ONE `DiagnosticAnalyzer` class, `CrossCuttingMagicStringLiteralAnalyzer`, covering all four call-site shapes with a single `DiagnosticDescriptor` — precedent set by SK0020/SK0021's `LoggingAuthoringStyleAnalyzer` for "one class, one platform standard," here narrowed further to "one class, one diagnostic ID, four trigger shapes" because all four are the same underlying rule ("never a raw literal at a cross-cutting call site") rather than four distinct standards.
2. The rule flags the LITERAL SYNTAX SHAPE, not any resolved value or declaring-class name — mirroring the acceptance-critical generality requirement already established for `NoBareHealthCheckLiteralWhereConstantsExistPredicate` (WO-028 P-178): the implementation MUST NOT contain any specific constants-class name (`WellKnownHeaders`, `SecurityClaimTypes`, `WebhookSignatureHeaders`, `HubGroupNaming`, etc.) as a string literal or type-name check anywhere in its logic. Any expression that is not itself a `StringLiteralExpression` at the checked argument/indexer-key position — an `IdentifierNameSyntax`, `MemberAccessExpressionSyntax` (`Foo.Bar`), or any other non-literal expression — passes clean, regardless of which class declares the referenced field. This is deliberately a syntax-shape check, not a value/identity check: the analyzer never needs to resolve what the referenced constant IS, only that the argument is NOT a bare literal.
3. Each of the four call-site shapes requires `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` to resolve the receiver/method/indexer to its EXACT `ContainingType`, following the SK0020 discipline (syntax-only simple-name matching on `SetTag`/`GetSection`/etc. would produce unacceptable false positives against unrelated types sharing those common method names):
   - HTTP header shapes: element-access (`headers["X"] = ...`) where the indexed expression's type is exactly `System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaders` (or a type in that inheritance chain — `HttpRequestHeaders`/`HttpResponseHeaders`/`HttpContentHeaders`) or `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.IHeaderDictionary`; plus invocations of `.Add`/`.TryAddWithoutValidation` resolved to the same containing types.
   - `Activity.SetBaggage`/`.SetTag`: invocation resolved to `System.Diagnostics.Activity.SetBaggage` or `System.Diagnostics.Activity.SetTag`.
   - `IConfiguration.GetSection`: invocation resolved to `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.IConfiguration.GetSection` (or its `ConfigurationExtensions` static-extension-method overload, both checked by `ContainingType` name).
   - `ClaimsPrincipal`/`Claim` comparison: a binary equality expression, `Claim.Type ==`/`.Equals(...)`, or a LINQ `.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Type == "...")`-shaped lambda predicate, where the compared member resolves to `System.Security.Claims.Claim.Type` or an invocation on `System.Security.Claims.ClaimsPrincipal`/`ClaimsIdentity` (`HasClaim`, `FindFirst`, `FindAll`) whose string argument is the checked position.
4. Diagnostic message text references BOTH remediation paths per the root `CLAUDE.md` decision guide, without asserting which applies (the analyzer cannot semantically distinguish a correlation/tenant literal from a domain-local one — that judgment is left to the developer): *"Raw string literal at a cross-cutting call site. Declare a named constant instead: use `SharedKernel.Primitives.CrossCutting.WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys` (`01.Core`) if this value is a platform-shared correlation/tenant identifier consumed across multiple domains, or a domain-local `static readonly`/`const` constants class (mirroring `SecurityClaimTypes`, `WebhookSignatureHeaders`, `HubGroupNaming`) if it is specific to this package."*
5. No namespace-scoped exemption — this rule fires globally like SK0014/SK0017–19, not with a suppression namespace like SK0001/SK0007/SK0013/SK0020/SK0021. A domain-local constants-holder class satisfies the rule by definition (it is referenced via `Identifier`/`MemberAccess`, never a literal at the call site) — there is no legitimate "exempt namespace" for a raw literal at any of these four call-site shapes.
6. `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` is a plain public helper class, NOT a `ConditionList`/`ICustomRule` — mirroring `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`'s precedent (WO-041 P-250): "no other assembly may declare its own independently-valued literal for a value `01.Core` already owns" is a cross-assembly, whole-platform invariant with no single-assembly "fire on one contrived violating assembly" shape. It reuses `StringConstantsClassDetector`'s field-shape + literal-value resolution technique (WO-028 P-178) — extended to walk EVERY `TypeDefinition` (not only `abstract sealed` "constants class" shapes) so a stray `const`/`static readonly string` field on an ordinary class is caught too — across a caller-supplied set of non-owning assemblies, and flags any resolved field value that matches a canonical value from a caller-supplied `IReadOnlyDictionary<string LogicalName, string Value>` (e.g. `{"CorrelationIdHeader": "X-Correlation-Id", "CorrelationIdBaggageKey": "correlation.id", ...}`), EXCLUDING fields declared on the owning type(s) themselves (matched by `TypeDefinition.FullName`, caller-supplied, e.g. `"SharedKernel.Primitives.CrossCutting.WellKnownHeaders"`/`"...WellKnownBaggageKeys"`).
7. `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion.AssertSoleDeclaration(IReadOnlyDictionary<string,string> canonicalValues, IReadOnlyCollection<string> owningTypeFullNames, IReadOnlyCollection<Assembly> assembliesToScan)` aggregates every violation found across the ENTIRE supplied assembly set before throwing (naming the offending declaring-type/field/value), mirroring `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`'s and `PipelineOrderAssertion`'s aggregate-failure-message convention. `00.Governance` never references `SharedKernel.Primitives` directly (it references nothing) — the consuming test project supplies `canonicalValues` and `owningTypeFullNames` itself, sourced from the real `WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys` values once `01.Core` C-43 ships.
8. **Real-assembly status:** this rule's real-assembly acceptance criterion CANNOT be verified today. As of this phase's authoring (2026-07-14), only `01.Core`'s D-30 design for `WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys` is locked (`01.Core/state-map.md`) — the C-43/T-34/DO-16 implementation has not shipped, and P-260/P-261/P-262/P-263 (the consuming-domain retrofits that would otherwise still be hand-rolling the correlation/tenant literals this rule watches for) have not landed either. Design, implementation, and tests for this phase use CONTRIVED in-memory multi-assembly Mono.Cecil fixtures only — the same "designed-ahead-of-a-pending-dependency" technique already used by `SK.00.ServiceDefaultsGovernance`, `SK.00.MetricsOutcomeTagAndMisregistrationGuard`, `SK.00.CryptoDelegationAndUowSeamGuard`, and `SK.00.LoggingStandardEnforcement`. Do not attempt a real-assembly wiring pass until `01.Core` C-43 ships AND P-260–P-263 land; track that as a follow-up, not a blocking condition on this phase's own completion.
9. SK0022 is the next sequential ID in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0021 was the prior ID). Targets `netstandard2.0`, pins `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 4.14.0` (no version change), zero new NuGet dependency. `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` reuses the existing `Mono.Cecil >= 0.11.5` reference in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` — zero new NuGet dependency there either.
10. Analyzer test fixtures for the four call-site shapes should use the in-compilation-stub technique established for SK0013/SK0020/SK0021 (declaring minimal self-contained stand-ins for `HttpHeaders`/`IHeaderDictionary`/`Activity`/`IConfiguration`/`ClaimsPrincipal` matching the real BCL namespace/type/member names) to avoid the same `CSharpAnalyzerTest` reference-assembly version-conflict class documented for SK0020/SK0021, rather than referencing the real `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Abstractions`/`System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource`/ASP.NET Core packages directly.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `Analyzers/CrossCuttingMagicStringLiteralAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0022 — bans a raw string literal at the four recognized cross-cutting call-site shapes |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/CrossCuttingMagicStringLiteralAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire-path tests (one per call-site shape) + pass-path tests (named-constant reference at each shape, including a fixture-local domain constants class) |
| `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | Cross-assembly assertion that no non-owning assembly redeclares a canonical `01.Core` cross-cutting literal value under a different name |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertionTests.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Create | Contrived multi-assembly fixtures: duplicate-value fire path, clean pass path (only the owning-type fixture declares the canonical values) |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | Diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] SK0022 fires on a raw string-literal argument at each of the four call-site shapes (HTTP header indexer/`.Add`/`.TryAddWithoutValidation`, `Activity.SetBaggage`/`.SetTag`, `IConfiguration.GetSection`, `ClaimsPrincipal`/`Claim` comparison), and does NOT fire when the argument is a reference to any named constant or `static readonly` field — including a fixture-local domain constants class distinct from any `01.Core` cross-cutting holder
- [ ] `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion.AssertSoleDeclaration` throws an aggregate exception naming the offending declaring-type/field/value when a contrived non-owning fixture assembly declares a field whose value matches a caller-supplied canonical value
- [ ] `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion.AssertSoleDeclaration` does not throw when only the owning-type fixture (standing in for `WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys`) declares the canonical values and no other fixture assembly duplicates them
- [ ] SK0022 and `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` are recorded in `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`'s diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, and implementation rules with the same structure as every prior SK entry
- [ ] Full `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests` and `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` suites remain green after the new tests land (baseline: 125/125 analyzer tests and 133/133 architecture tests as of `SK.00.LoggingStandardEnforcement` closeout)
- [ ] **Deferred, tracked explicitly, NOT gating this phase's own completion:** re-point `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` at the REAL `SharedKernel.Primitives` assembly (and every domain assembly retrofitted by P-260–P-263) once `01.Core` C-43/T-34/DO-16 ship — this is the acceptance criterion the phase input itself flags as unverifiable today

### Dependencies

- Depends on `01.Core` P-259 for **real-assembly verification only**: only D-30 (design) is locked in `01.Core/state-map.md` as of this phase's authoring (2026-07-14); C-43/T-34/DO-16 (the actual `WellKnownHeaders`/`WellKnownBaggageKeys` implementation) have not shipped. Not required for this phase's own design, implementation, or tests, which supply their own contrived canonical-value dictionaries and fixture assemblies standing in for the eventual owning type.
- Depends on `01.Core` P-260/P-261/P-262/P-263 for the SAME real-assembly-verification-only reason — these are the consuming-domain retrofit phases that would otherwise still be hand-rolling the correlation/tenant literals this rule watches for; until they land, real-assembly wiring would report a wall of pre-existing violations rather than validating the rule.
- Unblocks: gives the root `CLAUDE.md`'s implicit "declare cross-cutting magic strings as named constants" convention (reinforced by the `SecurityClaimTypes`/`WebhookSignatureHeaders`/`HubGroupNaming` precedent and the P-261 incident) a mechanical enforcement mechanism, mirroring SK0013 (raw `HttpClient`), `PresentationLayeringRules` (`ProblemDetails`/inline `Result`), and SK0020/SK0021 (ad hoc logging) — without this phase, the exact mismatch class P-261 exemplified (`"CorrelationId"` vs `"correlation.id"`) remains catchable only by architecture audit, not by PR-time CI.

### Tooling Version Notes

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp`: 4.14.0 (existing pin — SK0022 reuses it, no version change)
- `Mono.Cecil`: >= 0.11.5 (existing pin — `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` reuses it, no version change)
- Target framework: `netstandard2.0` (`SharedKernel.Analyzers`) / `net10.0` (`SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`)

<!-- phase-key: SK.00.StorageTopology -->
## Phase SK.00.StorageTopology — Governance: Architecture Enforcement for the 08.Storage Package Topology

### Goal

WO-043 (P-271) closes the enforcement gap for `08.Storage` the moment its first implementation phases (P-265/P-266/P-267) are dispatched, rather than retrofitting enforcement after a violation ships — the precedent every prior "prose rule decays without mechanical enforcement" incident in this platform has established (raw `HttpClient` P-159, inline `ProblemDetails` P-199, ad hoc logging P-250, magic-string P-264, and the direct precedent this phase mirrors, `RedisTopologyRules` P-145). `08.Storage/CLAUDE.md` already documents, in prose, that `SharedKernel.Storage.Abstractions` carries zero third-party NuGet dependencies, that `SharedKernel.Storage.S3` and `SharedKernel.Storage.Obs` are sibling packages that must never reference each other, that application code must never touch `Amazon.S3.*` directly, and that the provider `IAmazonS3` client is always a singleton. This phase ships one new NetArchTest rules class (`StorageTopologyRules`, three pure assembly-dependency-graph predicates, zero new Mono.Cecil technique) plus one new Roslyn analyzer (SK0023, the platform's first storage-domain diagnostic) enforcing the singleton-lifetime rule the same way SK0703 already enforces a DI-registration-lifetime shape for `IMessageBus`.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (one new analyzer class, one new diagnostic: SK0023); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (one new static rules class: `StorageTopologyRules`, no new `ICustomRule`/Mono.Cecil predicate — pure `NetArchTest` `.Should().NotHaveDependencyOn(...)` checks, mirroring `RedisTopologyRules`)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Analyzers/NonSingletonAmazonS3ClientRegistrationAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test files in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/StorageTopologyRules.cs`
  - Corresponding test files in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0023 | NonSingletonAmazonS3ClientRegistration | Usage | Warning | An `AddScoped`/`AddTransient` invocation (one- or two-type-argument form) whose first type argument's simple name is `IAmazonS3` |

### Implementation Rules

1. SK0023 is a syntax-only Roslyn analyzer — the structural inverse of SK0703 (`MessageBusSingletonRegistrationAnalyzer`, which flags `AddSingleton<IMessageBus>` because that type must be scoped). SK0023 flags `AddScoped`/`AddTransient` because `Amazon.S3.IAmazonS3` must always be singleton — thread-safe and connection/credential-pooled internally per the AWS SDK's own documented contract and `08.Storage/CLAUDE.md`'s explicit "Provider `IAmazonS3` clients are singletons" implementation rule. Type-argument extraction reuses SK0703's exact technique: `GenericNameSyntax.TypeArgumentList.Arguments[0]` as an `IdentifierNameSyntax`, simple-name exact match `"IAmazonS3"`. No `SemanticModel` required — the name is unique enough within DI-registration call sites that a syntax-only check carries negligible false-positive risk, consistent with SK0703/SK0705's cost-conscious precedent for `AddXxx<T>()` shape checks.
2. SK0023 fires globally with no suppression namespace — mirroring SK0703's and SK0014's "fires globally" convention, not a namespace-scoped trigger like SK0001/SK0007/SK0013/SK0020/SK0021. `IAmazonS3` must be a singleton wherever it is registered, not only inside `SharedKernel.Storage.S3`/`SharedKernel.Storage.Obs` — a consuming microservice that re-registers `IAmazonS3` directly (bypassing `AddSharedKernelS3Storage()`/`AddSharedKernelObsStorage()`) with the wrong lifetime is exactly as unsafe as the provider package itself getting it wrong.
3. `StorageTopologyRules` mirrors `RedisTopologyRules`'s structure and its documented `NotHaveDependencyOn` matching contract exactly (namespace `StartsWith`, no trailing dot, self-collision awareness) but is scoped to two provider packages instead of five:
   - `.AbstractionsHasNoThirdPartyDependencies(Assembly abstractionsAssembly) → ConditionList` — asserts `SharedKernel.Storage.Abstractions` has no dependency on `"Amazon"` (bare prefix — catches every `AWSSDK.S3` namespace, since its root namespace is `Amazon`), `"SharedKernel.Storage.S3"`, `"SharedKernel.Storage.Obs"`, or `"SharedKernel.Configuration"` (the Options-validation package only the two provider packages need). Four iterative `.Should().NotHaveDependencyOn(term)` calls, the same iterative pattern as `DomainLayerPurityRules.DomainAssembliesNeverReferenceInfrastructure` and `RedisTopologyRules.CachingAbstractionsHasNoInfrastructureDependencies`. None of the four terms is a prefix of `"SharedKernel.Storage.Abstractions"` — no self-collision.
   - `.ProviderPackagesNeverReferenceEachOther(Assembly s3Assembly, Assembly obsAssembly) → ConditionList[]` — returns exactly two elements: `[0]` asserts `SharedKernel.Storage.S3` has no dependency on `"SharedKernel.Storage.Obs"`; `[1]` asserts `SharedKernel.Storage.Obs` has no dependency on `"SharedKernel.Storage.S3"`. TWO NAMED `Assembly` parameters, not `params Assembly[]` — mirroring `UnitOfWorkSeamRules.UnitOfWorkInterfacesRemainDistinct`'s two-named-parameter convention, since the rule's whole purpose is comparing two specific, named packages. Unlike `RedisTopologyRules.CapabilityPackagesNeverReferenceEachOther` (which needs a `Dictionary<string,string[]>` to resolve each of FOUR scanned assemblies' own identifying term before excluding it to avoid self-collision), only two packages exist here and neither identifying namespace is a prefix of the other or of its own declaring assembly — no lookup table needed.
   - `.OnlyProviderPackagesMayReferenceAmazonS3(params Assembly[] assembliesUnderTest) → ConditionList` — asserts no type in the supplied assemblies has a dependency on `"Amazon.S3"`. Single `NotHaveDependencyOn` call — the structural sibling of `CompositionRootExclusivityRules.OnlyAllowedAssembliesMayReferenceConcreteProviders`/`CachingAbstractionRules.OnlyAllowedAssembliesMayReferenceConcreteCaching`. The caller must never include `SharedKernel.Storage.S3`/`SharedKernel.Storage.Obs` in the supplied list — exclusion is achieved entirely by caller choice, the same caller-controlled-exclusion convention as `PresentationLayeringRules` (there is no single internal namespace prefix that safely distinguishes "legitimate AWSSDK.S3 usage" from "leaked AWSSDK.S3 usage" other than which package the type lives in).
4. No new Mono.Cecil technique and no new `ICustomRule` — all three `StorageTopologyRules` factory methods are pure `NetArchTest` `.Should().NotHaveDependencyOn(...)` checks. Zero new NuGet dependency for either the analyzer (`Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` 4.14.0, existing pin) or the architecture-test rule (`NetArchTest.eNt` >= 1.3.2, existing pin).
5. **Real-assembly status — UNVERIFIABLE at authoring time (2026-07-16):** `08.Storage`'s own `state-map.md` shows every phase (Design through Published) at `○`/empty as of this phase's authoring — P-265 itself is only `◐` (Design in progress) per the root `state-map.md`, and P-266/P-267 have not started. `SharedKernel.Storage.Abstractions`, `.S3`, and `.Obs` do not exist as buildable assemblies yet. Design, implementation, and tests for this phase use CONTRIVED in-memory assemblies compiled via `CSharpCompilation` + `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage` — the same technique documented for `RedisTopologyRulesTests` and `CompositionRootExclusivityRulesTests` — following the identical "designed-ahead-of-a-pending-dependency" precedent already used by `SK.00.ServiceDefaultsGovernance`, `SK.00.MetricsOutcomeTagAndMisregistrationGuard`, `SK.00.CryptoDelegationAndUowSeamGuard`, and `SK.00.MagicStringGuard`. The phase input's own acceptance criterion — "All new architecture tests pass against the real built assemblies from P-266/P-267, not contrived fixtures only" — CANNOT be satisfied at design/implementation time; it is a post-P-266/P-267 follow-up gate, not a blocking condition on this phase's own completion.
6. SK0023 is the next sequential ID in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0022 was the prior ID) — a single-purpose, domain-adjacent rule following the SK0011/SK0013 precedent that not every domain-specific rule warrants its own ID block (02xx/03xx/07xx are reserved for multi-rule subsystem families: multi-tenancy, encryption, messaging; a lone storage rule stays in the sequential block rather than opening an "08xx" block for one ID).

### File-Level Plan

## Phase SK.00.SearchTopology — Governance: Architecture Enforcement for the 09.Search Topology <!-- phase-key: SK.00.SearchTopology -->

### Goal

WO-044 (P-278) closes the enforcement gap for `09.Search` the moment its first implementation phases (P-272/P-273/P-274) are dispatched, rather than retrofitting enforcement after a violation ships — the precedent this platform has established repeatedly (raw `HttpClient` P-159, inline `ProblemDetails` P-199, ad hoc logging P-250, magic-string P-264, and the direct precedent this phase mirrors, `RedisTopologyRules` P-145 / `StorageTopologyRules` P-271). `09.Search/CLAUDE.md` already documents, in prose, that `SharedKernel.Search.Abstractions` carries zero third-party NuGet dependencies (not even `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions`) and references only `SharedKernel.Primitives` (01.Core) and `SharedKernel.Contracts` (04.Contracts), that `SharedKernel.Search.Meilisearch` and `SharedKernel.Search.ElasticSearch` are sibling `.{Provider}` packages that must never reference each other, that `09.Search` as a whole may only reference `01.Core` and `04.Contracts`, that the EOL `NEST`/`Elasticsearch.Net` client packages are prohibited platform-wide, and that filter/query-builder field-name arguments must be `nameof()`-backed rather than raw string literals because a typo is a visible rejection on Meilisearch but a silent zero-result on ElasticSearch. This phase ships one new NetArchTest rules class (`SearchTopologyRules`, two pure assembly-dependency-graph predicates, zero new Mono.Cecil technique), one new method added to the existing `SharedKernelLayeringRules` class (`SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`), and two new Roslyn analyzers (SK0024, the platform's first refactor-safety/`nameof()`-encouragement rule, and SK0025, the platform's first EOL-third-party-package-prohibition rule).

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (two new analyzer classes, two new diagnostics: SK0024, SK0025); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (one new static rules class: `SearchTopologyRules` with two predicates; one new method added to the EXISTING `SharedKernelLayeringRules` class: `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0024_RawSearchFieldNameLiteralAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0025_ObsoleteElasticsearchClientUsageAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/SearchTopologyRules.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/SharedKernelLayeringRules.cs` (new `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` method); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/` (new test cases for the same); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0024 | RawSearchFieldNameLiteral | Usage | Warning | A raw string-literal argument at the field-name parameter position of one of eleven recognized `SharedKernel.Search.Abstractions` call-site shapes (`IQueryBuilder<TDocument>`.`OrderBy`/`OrderByDescending`/`SearchingIn`/`Faceting`/`WithNumericFacetStats`/`Returning`; `SearchFilter`.`Eq`/`Ne`/`In`/`Between`/`Exists`) |
| SK0025 | ObsoleteElasticsearchClientUsage | Usage | Warning | Any symbol usage (type, namespace, or `using` directive) whose resolved `ContainingAssembly.Name` is exactly `"NEST"` or `"Elasticsearch.Net"` |

### Implementation Rules

1. SK0024 and SK0025 are the next two sequential IDs in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0023 was the prior ID) and the platform's first `09.Search`-domain diagnostics. Both require `SemanticModel` resolution — SK0024 is the domain's eighth semantic-model analyzer (after SK0011, SK0015, SK0017–SK0019, SK0020, SK0022), SK0025 the ninth — because neither rule's discriminator is expressible as a safe syntax-only simple-name check without unacceptable false-positive risk (`OrderBy`/`Where`/`In`/`Exists` collide catastrophically with LINQ's own `Enumerable`/`Queryable` extension methods; `ElasticClient`/`ConnectionSettings` are generic enough names to plausibly exist in unrelated libraries).
2. SK0024 is the platform's first refactor-safety/`nameof()`-encouragement rule, distinct in INTENT from SK0022's cross-cutting-wire-contract magic-string prohibition even though both share the identical literal-vs-reference syntax-shape discriminator (`LiteralExpressionSyntax` of kind `StringLiteralExpression`, declaring-class-agnostic — a domain-local field-constants class satisfies the rule exactly as well as an inline `nameof(...)`, and the analyzer never inspects a resolved value). Do NOT merge SK0024 into SK0022's four call-site shapes or attempt to generalize SK0022 to cover it: SK0022 fires on genuinely cross-cutting/wire-contract literals (HTTP headers, OTel baggage, config sections, claim types); SK0024's motivating hazard — the Meilisearch-visible/ElasticSearch-silent typo asymmetry — is specific to `09.Search`'s two-provider query surface and is a different rationale that SK0022's own registry entry does not and should not reference.
3. SK0024's eleven recognized call-site shapes are six on `IQueryBuilder<TDocument>`/`SearchQueryBuilder<TDocument>` (`.OrderBy(string field)`, `.OrderByDescending(string field)`, `.SearchingIn(params string[] fields)`, `.Faceting(params string[] facetFields)`, `.WithNumericFacetStats(params string[] facetFields)`, `.Returning(params string[] fields)`) and five on `SearchFilter`'s static factories (`.Eq`, `.Ne`, `.In`, `.Between`, `.Exists`, field always at argument position 0), resolved via `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` against `SharedKernel.Search.Abstractions`'s exact declaring types. CONFIRM the concrete namespace of `IQueryBuilder<TDocument>`/`SearchQueryBuilder<TDocument>` (documented in `09.Search/CLAUDE.md` as living under a `Querying/` folder — the exact namespace segment is not yet locked as of this phase's authoring, since `09.Search`'s own Design task D-09 is still `○`) at implementation time, once P-272 ships real source. For the four `params string[]` shapes, the analyzer must walk EVERY argument expression at that parameter position individually — both the multi-argument call form (`SearchingIn("a", "b")`) and any array/collection-expression form.
4. `SearchTopologyRules` mirrors `StorageTopologyRules`'s structure and its documented `NotHaveDependencyOn` matching contract exactly (namespace `StartsWith`, no trailing dot, self-collision awareness) but is scoped to `09.Search`'s two SIBLING provider packages (`SharedKernel.Search.Meilisearch`/`.ElasticSearch`, mirroring `08.Storage`'s `.S3`/`.Obs` sibling-not-`.Core`-split precedent exactly, per `09.Search/CLAUDE.md`'s own explicit rejection of a `SharedKernel.Search.Core`). `.AbstractionsHasNoThirdPartyDependencies` carries a SIXTH forbidden term (`"Microsoft.Extensions"`) beyond `StorageTopologyRules`'s five-term analog, because `09.Search/CLAUDE.md` documents `SharedKernel.Search.Abstractions` as having a stricter dependency posture than `SharedKernel.Storage.Abstractions` — zero `PackageReference` of any kind, not even `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` (which `SharedKernel.Caching.Abstractions` IS permitted). No new Mono.Cecil technique and no new `ICustomRule` — pure `NetArchTest` checks, zero new NuGet dependency.
5. `SharedKernelLayeringRules.SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` is the first method on `SharedKernelLayeringRules` to return `ConditionList[]` instead of a single `ConditionList` — every sibling method on that class predates the newer domain-boundary-rule-class convention (`RedisTopologyRules`/`CommunicationLayeringRules`/`StorageTopologyRules`) of returning one `ConditionList` per forbidden term for per-term failure-message granularity. This method deliberately follows that newer convention because it is the first `SharedKernelLayeringRules` method checking against more than two or three forbidden terms (fifteen — one per every OTHER numbered domain's package family). Document any future simplification to a single `.NotHaveDependencyOnAny(string[])` call (if confirmed available in the pinned `NetArchTest.eNt` version) here before applying it, and only if it preserves per-term failure-message granularity.
6. The fifteen-term forbidden list inside `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` is an EXPLICIT enumeration, not a derived/reflective one — per this file's own long-standing Implementation Rule ("Architecture tests in `SharedKernelLayeringRules` must mirror the layering table in the root `CLAUDE.md` exactly. If a new domain (folder XX) is added, the layering rules must be updated in the same PR"), a future `18.NewDomain` addition MUST append its package-family namespace term to this list in the SAME PR that adds the new domain. `"SharedKernel.AI"` (not `"SharedKernel.Intelligence"`) is the correct term for `10.Intelligence` — confirmed against the root `CLAUDE.md` Abstractions table (`SharedKernel.AI.Abstractions` / `.VectorDb`), the one term in the list that does not match its folder name.
7. Real-assembly status for SK0024/SK0025/`SearchTopologyRules`/`SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` — UNVERIFIABLE at authoring time (2026-07-19), and UNLIKE every prior "designed-ahead-of-a-pending-dependency" precedent in this domain, the WO-044 phase input's own acceptance criteria make real-assembly verification a GATING condition on this phase's completion, not a non-blocking follow-up (see Acceptance Criteria below). `09.Search`'s own `state-map.md` shows the entire Design phase (D-01 through D-28, covering P-272/P-273/P-274) at `○` as of this phase's authoring; only bare `.csproj` skeletons (zero references, zero content) exist on disk for all three packages. Design, implementation, and initial tests for this phase use CONTRIVED in-memory assemblies via `CSharpCompilation` + `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage` (the `RedisTopologyRulesTests`/`StorageTopologyRulesTests` technique); the real-assembly re-verification pass against P-272/P-273/P-274's shipped output MUST be completed, and its own acceptance-criterion checkbox explicitly closed, before this phase can be marked fully `●` complete.

## Phase SK.00.IntelligenceTopology — Governance: Architecture Enforcement for the 10.Intelligence Package Topology <!-- phase-key: SK.00.IntelligenceTopology -->

### Goal

WO-045 (P-286) closes the enforcement gap for `10.Intelligence` the moment its first implementation phases (P-279/P-280/P-281/P-282) ship real code, mirroring the exact precedent this platform has now established four times running (`RedisTopologyRules` P-145, `CommunicationLayeringRules` P-159/P-167, `StorageTopologyRules` P-271, `SearchTopologyRules` P-278). `10.Intelligence/CLAUDE.md` already documents, in prose, that `SharedKernel.AI.Abstractions` carries zero third-party NuGet dependencies (only `SharedKernel.Primitives`, and `SharedKernel.Contracts` if genuinely needed, as `ProjectReference`s), that the three sibling provider packages (`SharedKernel.AI.Qdrant`, `.Milvus`, `.SemanticKernel`) must never reference each other in either direction, that `10.Intelligence` as a whole may only reference `01.Core` and `04.Contracts`, that the domain ships no `IHealthCheck` and references `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks` nowhere, that injecting a raw model SDK or vector-DB client type (`QdrantClient`, `MilvusClient`, `Kernel`) is a hard violation unless routed through the documented three-gate escape-hatch pattern, and that bare string literals for model identifiers and collection/field names are prohibited alongside SK0022's existing shapes. This phase ships one new NetArchTest rules class (`IntelligenceTopologyRules`, three pure assembly-dependency-graph predicates, zero new Mono.Cecil technique — the first THREE-named-Assembly-parameter sibling-non-reference check in this domain, since 10.Intelligence has three sibling providers rather than two), one new method added to the existing `SharedKernelLayeringRules` class (`IntelligenceReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`), and two new Roslyn analyzers (SK0026, the platform's first raw-vector-DB/model-SDK-client-injection prohibition, and SK0027, a `nameof()`-encouragement rule for collection/field/model-identifier literals, structurally parallel to SK0024 but grounded in this domain's own sharper hazard — a copy-pasted, typo'd `embeddingModelId` literal reproduces Domain Invariant #1's "no engine can detect a model-identity mismatch" failure mode with no engine-visible error at all).

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (two new analyzer classes, two new diagnostics: SK0026, SK0027); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (one new static rules class: `IntelligenceTopologyRules` with three predicates; one new method added to the EXISTING `SharedKernelLayeringRules` class: `IntelligenceReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0026_RawIntelligenceProviderClientConstructorInjectionAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0027_RawIntelligenceIdentifierLiteralAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/IntelligenceTopologyRules.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/SharedKernelLayeringRules.cs` (new `IntelligenceReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` method); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/` (new test cases for the same); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0026 | RawIntelligenceProviderClientConstructorInjection | Usage | Warning | A constructor parameter resolved (via `SemanticModel`) to exactly `Qdrant.Client.QdrantClient`, `Milvus.Client.MilvusClient`, or `Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Kernel`, outside that type's own owning provider package |
| SK0027 | RawIntelligenceIdentifierLiteral | Usage | Warning | A raw string-literal argument at the collection-name/field-name/embedding-model-id parameter position of one of eight recognized `SharedKernel.AI.Abstractions` call-site shapes (`VectorFilter.Eq`/`Ne`/`In`/`Between`/`Exists`; `IVectorCollectionProvisioner.CollectionExistsAsync`/`DeleteCollectionAsync`/`ProbeAsync`; `VectorCollectionDefinition.Create`; `VectorCollectionDefinitionBuilder.EmbeddingModel`/`Field`) |

### Implementation Rules

1. SK0026 and SK0027 are the next two sequential IDs in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0025 was the prior ID) and the platform's first `10.Intelligence`-domain diagnostics. SK0026 requires `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` exact-full-type-name resolution — not the syntax-only simple-name match SK0013 uses for `HttpClient` — because `Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Kernel`'s simple name `"Kernel"` is highly collision-prone (a convolution kernel, an OS-kernel abstraction, a compute-shader kernel are all plausible unrelated types named `Kernel` elsewhere in a consuming service's own dependency graph); the analyzer resolves all three client types (`QdrantClient`, `MilvusClient`, `Kernel`) uniformly via the semantic model for implementation consistency even though `QdrantClient`/`MilvusClient` alone would likely be safe as syntax-only checks. SK0027 requires `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` for the same reason SK0024 does — the eight call-site method names (`Eq`, `Ne`, `In`, `Field`, etc.) are common enough to collide with unrelated types without an exact-declaring-type check. SK0026 is this domain's tenth semantic-model analyzer (after SK0011, SK0015, SK0017–SK0019, SK0020, SK0022, SK0024, SK0025); SK0027 is the eleventh.
2. SK0026's namespace exemption mirrors SK0013's/SK0007's established `SyntaxNode.Parent` ancestor-namespace-walk pattern, keyed per matched client type: a `QdrantClient` parameter is exempt only inside a namespace starting with `SharedKernel.AI.Qdrant`; `MilvusClient` only inside `SharedKernel.AI.Milvus`; `Kernel` only inside `SharedKernel.AI.SemanticKernel`. There is no cross-exemption — a `QdrantClient` parameter inside `SharedKernel.AI.Milvus` still fires, since that would itself be a sibling-package violation the topology rules independently catch at the assembly level.
3. SK0027 is structurally parallel to SK0024 (`RawSearchFieldNameLiteral`) — same literal-vs-reference syntax-shape discriminator (`LiteralExpressionSyntax` of kind `StringLiteralExpression`, declaring-class-agnostic: a `nameof(...)` expression or a domain-local identifier-constants class member passes automatically, regardless of which class declares it) — but its motivating hazard is DIFFERENT from and sharper than SK0024's, and the two entries must not cross-reference each other's rationale, the same discipline already established between SK0022 and SK0024. SK0024's hazard is an engine-VISIBILITY asymmetry (Meilisearch rejects, ElasticSearch silently zero-results). SK0027's sharper hazard is that a `VectorCollectionDefinition.Create(name, embeddingModelId, ...)` call and the record/query call sites that must independently supply the SAME `embeddingModelId` string have NO shared compile-time link — if a typo'd literal is copy-pasted identically at both places, `IVectorRecord.ModelId == VectorCollectionDefinition.EmbeddingModelId` passes the mismatch guard cleanly and the corpus is silently embedded/queried under a phantom model-identity string with zero engine-detectable error, on BOTH Qdrant and Milvus — Domain Invariant #1's exact "no engine can detect a model-identity mismatch" hazard, reproduced by a literal-copy-paste-typo instead of a genuine two-model mixup.
4. SK0027's eight recognized call-site shapes are five on `VectorFilter`'s static factories (`.Eq`, `.Ne`, `.In`, `.Between`, `.Exists`, field always at argument position 0 — the structural twin of SK0024's five `SearchFilter` shapes) and three on `IVectorCollectionProvisioner` (`.CollectionExistsAsync(string collectionName, ct)`, `.DeleteCollectionAsync(string collectionName, ct)`, `.ProbeAsync(string collectionName, ct)`, `collectionName` always position 0), PLUS both string parameters of `VectorCollectionDefinition.Create(string name, string embeddingModelId, int dimension, VectorDistanceMetric metric, IReadOnlyList<VectorFieldDefinition> fields)` checked independently (position 0 `name` AND position 1 `embeddingModelId`), PLUS `VectorCollectionDefinitionBuilder.EmbeddingModel(string modelId, int dimension)` (position 0) and `.Field(string name, VectorFieldKind kind, bool filterable = false)` (position 0) — resolved via `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` against `SharedKernel.AI.Abstractions`'s exact declaring types. `VectorCollectionCutoverRequest.StagingCollectionName`/`.LiveCollectionName` are object-initializer PROPERTY assignments, not method-call arguments, and are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this rule's call-site-argument-position detection technique — the same documented method-call-only limitation SK0024 carries, not attempted here either.
5. `IntelligenceTopologyRules` (WO-045 P-286) mirrors `StorageTopologyRules`/`SearchTopologyRules`'s structure and documented `NotHaveDependencyOn` matching contract exactly (namespace `StartsWith`, no trailing dot, self-collision awareness) but is scoped to THREE sibling provider packages, not two — `SharedKernel.AI.Qdrant`, `.Milvus`, `.SemanticKernel`, per `10.Intelligence/CLAUDE.md`'s own explicit statement that "no `.Core` is extracted to share implementation shape between them — duplication ... is deliberate, mirroring the `09.Search` precedent exactly." `.AbstractionsHasNoThirdPartyDependencies` carries EIGHT forbidden terms (two more than `SearchTopologyRules`'s six) — three bare-prefix third-party-SDK terms (`"Qdrant"`, `"Milvus"`, `"Microsoft.SemanticKernel"`) instead of two, plus three `"SharedKernel.AI.{Provider}"` sibling-package terms instead of two, plus `"SharedKernel.Configuration"` and `"Microsoft.Extensions"` carried over unchanged from the `SearchTopologyRules` precedent (10.Intelligence/CLAUDE.md's own Hard Violations list states the same zero-`PackageReference`-beyond-`SharedKernel.Primitives`/`.Contracts` posture verbatim). No new Mono.Cecil technique and no new `ICustomRule` — pure `NetArchTest` checks, zero new NuGet dependency.
6. `IntelligenceTopologyRules.ProviderPackagesNeverReferenceEachOther(Assembly qdrantAssembly, Assembly milvusAssembly, Assembly semanticKernelAssembly)` is the FIRST three-named-Assembly-parameter shape in this domain — every prior sibling-non-reference predicate (`StorageTopologyRules`, `SearchTopologyRules`, `UnitOfWorkSeamRules.UnitOfWorkInterfacesRemainDistinct`) uses exactly two named parameters, because Storage and Search each have exactly two sibling providers. Returns `ConditionList[]` with SIX elements (each of the three packages checked against each of the other two, in the order Qdrant→Milvus, Qdrant→SemanticKernel, Milvus→Qdrant, Milvus→SemanticKernel, SemanticKernel→Qdrant, SemanticKernel→Milvus) — no `Dictionary<string,string[]>` lookup table is needed (unlike `RedisTopologyRules`'s four-package case), since none of the three identifying namespaces (`"SharedKernel.AI.Qdrant"`, `"SharedKernel.AI.Milvus"`, `"SharedKernel.AI.SemanticKernel"`) is a prefix of another or of its own declaring assembly. Caller must assert `.GetResult().IsSuccessful` on EACH of the six elements.
7. `IntelligenceTopologyRules.NoHealthChecksDependencyAcrossIntelligencePackages(params Assembly[] intelligenceAssemblies)` uses the NARROW term `"Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks"` — deliberately NOT the bare `"Microsoft.Extensions"` prefix `.AbstractionsHasNoThirdPartyDependencies` uses — because the three PROVIDER packages legitimately need OTHER `Microsoft.Extensions.*` packages (`DependencyInjection`, `Options`, `Logging`) for their DI wiring; only `SharedKernel.AI.Abstractions` itself carries the zero-`Microsoft.Extensions`-anything posture. This mechanizes Domain Invariant #8 / `10.Intelligence/CLAUDE.md`'s own Hard Violations entry verbatim: "Implementing `IHealthCheck`, or referencing `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks`, anywhere in `10.Intelligence`."
8. `SharedKernelLayeringRules.IntelligenceReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` follows `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`'s `ConditionList[]`-per-forbidden-term convention exactly, with the SAME fifteen-term count — the forbidden list swaps `"SharedKernel.Search"` IN (09.Search is now a forbidden reference for 10.Intelligence) and `"SharedKernel.AI"` OUT (10.Intelligence is now the domain under test, excluded from its own forbidden list by omission, not by an explicit self-exclusion term). Every other term is unchanged from `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`'s own list. A future `18.NewDomain` addition MUST append its package-family term to BOTH this method's list AND `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`'s list (and any future sibling of this shape) in the SAME PR that adds the new domain, per this file's long-standing Implementation Rule.
9. Real-assembly status for SK0026/SK0027/`IntelligenceTopologyRules`/`IntelligenceReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` — UNVERIFIABLE at authoring time (2026-07-21), and following the `SK.00.SearchTopology` precedent (not the older non-blocking-follow-up precedent), the WO-045 phase input's own acceptance criteria make real-assembly verification a GATING condition on this phase's completion. `10.Intelligence/CLAUDE.md` states explicitly: "No production `.cs` file has been written yet... On disk today there is still only the original placeholder inventory" — `SharedKernel.AI.Abstractions`'s interface CONTRACT is ratified (P-279's Design phase), but its Scaffold/Core/Tests/Docs/Published phases, and all of P-280/P-281/P-282, are `○ Not started` per `10.Intelligence/state-map.md`. Design, implementation, and initial tests for this phase use CONTRIVED in-memory assemblies via `CSharpCompilation` + `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage` (the `RedisTopologyRulesTests`/`StorageTopologyRulesTests`/`SearchTopologyRulesTests` technique); the real-assembly re-verification pass against P-279/P-280/P-281/P-282's shipped output MUST be completed, and its own acceptance-criterion checkbox explicitly closed, before this phase can be marked fully `●` complete — see Acceptance Criteria and Dependencies below.

## Phase SK.00.WorkflowTopology — Governance: Architecture Enforcement for 17.Workflows (Topology + Determinism Analyzers) <!-- phase-key: SK.00.WorkflowTopology -->

### Goal

WO-046 (P-290) closes the enforcement gap for `17.Workflows` the moment its Scaffold/Core phases ship real code, mirroring the exact precedent this platform has now established five times running (`RedisTopologyRules` P-145, `CommunicationLayeringRules` P-159/P-167, `StorageTopologyRules` P-271, `SearchTopologyRules` P-278, `IntelligenceTopologyRules` P-286). `17.Workflows/CLAUDE.md` already documents, in prose, every rule this phase mechanizes: that `SharedKernel.Workflows.Temporal` may only reference `01.Core`, `04.Contracts`, and `05.Application`; that `ITemporalRawClientAccessor` is gated three ways and no in-repo type may consume it; that the package must never implement `IHealthCheck` or reference `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks`; that a `[Workflow]`-attributed type must never call a non-deterministic or side-effecting API (`DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`/`DateTime.Now`, `Guid.NewGuid()`, `new Random()`, `Task.Run`/`Task.Delay`/`ConfigureAwait(false)`, `Environment.*`/`File.*`, or inject `IClock`/`ILogger<T>`) while the identical APIs remain correct — in some cases mandatory — inside an `ActivityBase`-derived type; and that injecting a raw `ITemporalClient`/`TemporalWorker`/`WorkflowHandle` into application code outside `SharedKernel.Workflows.Temporal` is a hard violation. The consequence of a leak here is uniquely severe among every prior "documented but unenforced" precedent this platform has closed: a non-deterministic API compiled cleanly into a workflow body passes every unit test and fails only on replay, in production, at an arbitrary future time, taking down every in-flight execution of that workflow type simultaneously — the domain's own brain calls the first analyzer in this phase "the highest-value analyzer this domain can have" for exactly this reason. This phase ships one new NetArchTest rules class (`WorkflowTopologyRules`, two predicates — the first `*TopologyRules` class in this domain scoped to a domain with no sibling provider packages), one new method added to the existing `SharedKernelLayeringRules` class (`WorkflowsReferencesOnlyCoreContractsAndApplication` — the first layering-boundary method on that class permitting three upstream domains rather than two), and two new Roslyn analyzers (SK0028, the platform's first non-deterministic-API-inside-workflow prohibition and the first analyzer in this domain scoped by type attribution/inheritance rather than namespace; and SK0029, a raw Temporal client-injection prohibition structurally identical to SK0013/SK0026).

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (two new analyzer classes, two new diagnostics: SK0028, SK0029); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (one new static rules class: `WorkflowTopologyRules` with two predicates; one new method added to the EXISTING `SharedKernelLayeringRules` class: `WorkflowsReferencesOnlyCoreContractsAndApplication`)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0028_NonDeterministicApiUsageInsideWorkflowAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0029_RawTemporalClientConstructorInjectionAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/WorkflowTopologyRules.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoRawClientAccessorConsumptionPredicate.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/SharedKernelLayeringRules.cs` (new `WorkflowsReferencesOnlyCoreContractsAndApplication` method); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/` (new test cases for the same); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0028 | NonDeterministicApiUsageInsideWorkflow | Design | Warning | Inside a `[Workflow]`-attributed or `WorkflowBase`-derived type (never inside an `ActivityBase`-derived type), any of: `DateTime.UtcNow`/`.Now`, `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`/`.Now`, `Guid.NewGuid()`, `new Random()`, `Task.Run`/`.Delay`/`ConfigureAwait(false)`, `Environment.*`/`File.*` member access, or a constructor parameter typed `IClock`/`ILogger<T>` |
| SK0029 | RawTemporalClientConstructorInjection | Usage | Warning | A constructor parameter resolved (via `SemanticModel`) to `Temporalio.Client.ITemporalClient`, `Temporalio.Client.TemporalClient`, `Temporalio.Worker.TemporalWorker`, or `Temporalio.Client.WorkflowHandle`, outside a namespace starting with `SharedKernel.Workflows.Temporal` |

### Implementation Rules

1. SK0028 and SK0029 are the next two sequential IDs in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0027 was the prior ID) and the platform's first `17.Workflows`-domain diagnostics; following the `SK0011`/`SK0013`/`SK0023` precedent, no new `17xx` block is opened. SK0028 is this domain's twelfth semantic-model analyzer; SK0029 is the thirteenth.
2. SK0028 is the first analyzer in this domain to scope its trigger by TYPE ATTRIBUTION/INHERITANCE (a `[Workflow]` attribute resolved to `Temporalio.Workflows.WorkflowAttribute`, or `WorkflowBase` anywhere in the base-type chain) rather than the established namespace-ancestor `SyntaxNode.Parent` walk every prior namespace-scoped SK analyzer uses. The `ActivityBase`/`[Activity]` exclusion is checked FIRST, as a hard positive exclusion, not merely "outside the trigger-in scope" — every one of SK0028's seven forbidden shapes is correct, and in the case of `IClock`/`ILogger<T>` injection actually MANDATORY, inside an activity (per `SK0001`). This is the platform's first analyzer explicitly encoding a per-API-shape INVERSION of another rule's own trigger condition.
3. SK0028's seven forbidden shapes are fixed by this phase's own acceptance criteria: the four-property clock set (`DateTime.UtcNow`/`.Now`, `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`/`.Now` — reusing `DoesNotCallSystemClockPredicate`'s exact property list, resolved here via `SemanticModel` instead of IL), `Guid.NewGuid()`, `new Random()`, the `Task.Run`/`Task.Delay`/`ConfigureAwait(false)` scheduler-escape trio, `Environment.*`/`File.*` member access, and constructor-injected `IClock`/`ILogger<T>`. `HttpClient` and general I/O are documented `17.Workflows/CLAUDE.md` Hard Violations too but are deliberately NOT part of this rule's trigger set — extending detection to them is a candidate follow-up, not attempted here.
4. SK0029 mirrors SK0013's single-shared-namespace-exemption shape (one term, `SharedKernel.Workflows.Temporal`) rather than SK0026's per-client-type/per-owning-package exemption mapping (three terms) — because 17.Workflows has exactly one owning package, not three sibling providers.
5. `WorkflowTopologyRules` (WO-046 P-290) is the first `*TopologyRules` class in this domain scoped to a domain with NO sibling provider packages — a single package, `SharedKernel.Workflows.Temporal`, is both the abstraction surface and the Temporal-specific implementation, so this class carries no `AbstractionsHasNoThirdPartyDependencies`/`ProviderPackagesNeverReferenceEachOther` pair. Its two methods are single-package analogues of the concerns those sibling-domain classes address differently: `.NoRawClientAccessorConsumptionInRepo(params Assembly[])` mechanizes gate 3 of the documented three-gate `ITemporalRawClientAccessor` escape hatch (no in-repo type may consume the accessor as a constructor parameter or field — an absolute, literal "no type inside this repo" prohibition, NOT a per-consuming-microservice correlation with whether `.AllowRawClientAccess()` was called, which is out of a platform-level architecture test's jurisdiction); `.NoHealthChecksDependencyInWorkflows(Assembly)` mirrors `IntelligenceTopologyRules.NoHealthChecksDependencyAcrossIntelligencePackages`'s narrow-term precedent (`"Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks"` only, not the bare `"Microsoft.Extensions"` prefix, since the package legitimately needs `Hosting`/`DependencyInjection`/`Logging`/`Options`).
6. `SharedKernelLayeringRules.WorkflowsReferencesOnlyCoreContractsAndApplication(Assembly)` is the first layering-boundary method on that class permitting THREE upstream domains (`01.Core`, `04.Contracts`, `05.Application`) rather than two. Its forbidden-term list is therefore FOURTEEN terms, not the fifteen `SearchReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts`/`IntelligenceReferencesOnlyCoreAndContracts` each use: `"SharedKernel.Caching"`, `"SharedKernel.Domain"`, `"SharedKernel.Persistence"`, `"SharedKernel.Messaging"`, `"SharedKernel.Storage"`, `"SharedKernel.Search"`, `"SharedKernel.AI"`, `"SharedKernel.Communication"`, `"SharedKernel.Security"`, `"SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults"`, `"SharedKernel.MultiTenancy"`, `"SharedKernel.Presentation"`, `"SharedKernel.Integration"`, `"SharedKernel.Testing"` — with `"SharedKernel.Application"` the one term deliberately ABSENT versus its two siblings' lists (self-term `"SharedKernel.Workflows"` is excluded by omission, the same convention as every prior sibling). Returns `ConditionList[]` (fourteen elements), following the same convention as its two siblings.
7. Real-assembly status — UNVERIFIABLE at authoring time (2026-07-22), and, following the `SK.00.SearchTopology`/`SK.00.IntelligenceTopology` precedent, real-assembly verification is a GATING condition on this phase's completion, not a non-blocking follow-up. `17.Workflows/state-map.md` shows its entire Design/Scaffold/Core phases at `○` as of this phase's authoring — no production `.cs` file has shipped for `SharedKernel.Workflows.Temporal`. Design, implementation, and initial tests for this phase use CONTRIVED in-memory assemblies via `CSharpCompilation` + `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage` (the established multi-phase technique).
