## Phase SK.00.ResultDiscardGuard — Governance: Roslyn Analyzer for Result/Result\<T\> Discard-Detection <!-- phase-key: SK.00.ResultDiscardGuard -->

### Goal

WO-049 (P-299) closes what the phase input itself calls "the single highest-leverage gold-standard governance gap in the entire platform relative to its cost." `Result<T>` is the platform's sole sanctioned error-handling primitive, used by every domain from `03.Domain` through `17.Workflows` — its entire value proposition is that callers must explicitly branch on outcome instead of exceptions silently unwinding the stack. That proposition is completely defeated the moment a caller invokes a `Result`/`Result<T>`-returning member as a bare statement and never inspects `.IsSuccess`/`.IsFailure`: it compiles cleanly, produces no compiler warning, and the failure path is simply gone — exactly as dangerous as a fire-and-forgotten `Task` (CS4014), one level further down the stack. `01.Core`'s `IHasSuccessFlag` zero-member marker interface (P-230, WO-038) was added to `SharedKernel.Primitives.Results` specifically to enable this class of reflection-free, interface-based static analysis and has sat unused for this purpose since. This phase ships exactly one new Roslyn analyzer (SK0030) and no new `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` artifact — detecting a bare-statement discard is inherently a per-syntax-tree, per-compilation-unit concern the analyzer resolves completely inside each consuming project's own build, with no assembly-dependency-graph or IL-level aspect any `ICustomRule`/`ConditionList` predicate could usefully add. The rule's structural design is unusually cheap for what it buys: registering on exactly two `ExpressionStatementSyntax` child shapes (`InvocationExpressionSyntax`, `AwaitExpressionSyntax`) and NEVER inspecting `AssignmentExpressionSyntax` at all makes every one of the phase input's required non-firing shapes — assignment to a variable/field, and explicit discard via `_ = ...` — fall out of the same single structural exclusion, with zero dedicated `IDiscardSymbol` semantic-model detection needed. This phase is also the first in this domain whose "real-assembly"-style verification pass audits ALREADY-SHIPPED code across other domains (`05.Application.Behaviors`, `06.Persistence.EfCore`, `07.Messaging.MassTransit`, `17.Workflows.Temporal` — all four Published as of this phase's authoring) rather than waiting on a not-yet-implemented dependency; per this domain's own Test Rules ("never test analyzers by compiling real source files manually"), that audit is executed as a manual/tool-assisted review producing representative fixtures modeled on each distinct real consumption shape found, not a literal file-I/O read of real `.cs` files into a test compilation.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (one new analyzer class, one new diagnostic: SK0030)
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0030_ResultOutcomeDiscardedAnalyzer.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/`
- Modified files: `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0030 | ResultOutcomeDiscarded | Usage | Warning | A bare `ExpressionStatementSyntax` wrapping an `InvocationExpressionSyntax` or `AwaitExpressionSyntax` whose `SemanticModel`-resolved type implements `SharedKernel.Primitives.Results.IHasSuccessFlag` (i.e., is `Result`/`Result<T>`) — the outcome is produced and immediately thrown away. `AssignmentExpressionSyntax` (covering both a real re-assignment and an explicit `_ = ...` discard) is never inspected, so both pass structurally with no dedicated discard-detection logic. |

### Implementation Rules

1. SK0030 `ResultOutcomeDiscardedAnalyzer` is the next sequential ID in the SK0001–SK00N general-purpose block (SK0029 was the prior ID). It registers on exactly two `SyntaxKind`s — the `ExpressionStatement`'s `InvocationExpressionSyntax`/`AwaitExpressionSyntax` child shapes — and deliberately never inspects `AssignmentExpressionSyntax` at all. This single structural exclusion is what makes BOTH the "assigned to a variable/field" pass case and the "explicit discard `_ = ...`" pass case fall out for free, with zero `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo`/`IDiscardSymbol` check needed — a cheaper and simpler design than a naive first pass would produce.
2. SK0030's interface match uses the same "simple name + `ContainingNamespace` prefix" discriminator established by SK0017–SK0019 (`"IHasSuccessFlag"` + `"SharedKernel.Primitives"` prefix, matching the real type's actual home at `SharedKernel.Primitives.Results.IHasSuccessFlag` — confirmed by reading the shipped `01.Core` source, not assumed) rather than an exact-assembly `INamedTypeSymbol` identity check, for the same reason SK0017–SK0019 chose it: analyzer test fixtures can declare a fixture-local `IHasSuccessFlag`-named interface inside a matching-namespace code block in the SAME test compilation, with no `ProjectReference` to the real `SharedKernel.Primitives` assembly required for fire/pass-path unit tests. The check walks `INamedTypeSymbol.AllInterfaces` (plus the resolved type itself) — never a `BaseList`/syntax-only check — since `Result`/`Result<T>` and any consumer-defined `IHasSuccessFlag` implementor may satisfy the interface transitively.
3. For the `AwaitExpressionSyntax` shape, `SemanticModel.GetTypeInfo(awaitExpressionSyntax)` already returns Roslyn's own unwrapped "what does `await x` evaluate to" type — no manual `Task<T>`/`ValueTask<T>` unwrapping logic is written or needed. This is what makes `await FooAsync();` as a bare statement (where `FooAsync` returns `Task<Result<T>>`/`ValueTask<Result<T>>`) resolve directly to `Result<T>` and correctly FIRE — the documented edge case explicitly called out by this phase's own acceptance criteria, and the CS4014 analogy one level further down: an awaited-but-unobserved `Result` outcome is exactly as dangerous as an unawaited `Task`.
4. SK0030 only ever inspects the OUTERMOST `ExpressionStatementSyntax.Expression`'s resolved type — never a nested sub-expression's type. This single design choice is what makes "passed as an argument" (`Bar(Foo());`, outer type is `Bar`'s return type) and "receiver of a member-access/method chain" (`Foo().Match(...);`, outer type is `Match`'s return type) both pass without any special-case logic — while a fluent chain whose OUTERMOST call still resolves to an `IHasSuccessFlag`-implementing type (`Foo().Map(x => x + 1);`, where `Map` itself returns `Result<TNew>`) correctly still FIRES, since the chain's final produced `Result` is genuinely, separately discarded. Document this nuance explicitly in the analyzer's XML doc and in the pass/fire test pair (T-263/T-257) so a future reader does not "fix" the fire case as a false positive.
5. SK0030 deliberately does NOT register on `ObjectCreationExpressionSyntax` (`Result`/`Result<T>` in this platform are produced exclusively via static factory methods — `Result.Success()`/`Result<T>.Failure(...)` — never a public constructor call) or on `ConditionalAccessExpressionSyntax` (`maybeService?.ReturnsResult();`). Both are documented, deliberate scope limitations for this phase — accepted false-negative risk, mirroring this domain's established `SK0708`/`HealthCheckTagIntegrityRules`/`NoTaskDelayOutsideResilienceBehaviorPredicate` "document the limitation, revisit only on a real finding" discipline — not oversights.
6. SK0030 has NO `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` counterpart. Unlike every `*TopologyRules`-style phase in this file, a bare-statement `Result` discard is inherently a per-syntax-tree, per-compilation-unit concern the Roslyn analyzer already resolves completely inside each consuming project's own build — there is no assembly-dependency-graph or IL-level aspect to this rule an `ICustomRule`/`ConditionList` predicate could usefully add.
7. Real-source verification: SK0030 is the platform's first analyzer whose "GATING, not deferred" verification pass audits ALREADY-SHIPPED code across other domains (`05.Application.Behaviors`, `06.Persistence.EfCore`, `07.Messaging.MassTransit`, `17.Workflows.Temporal` — all four already Published as of this phase's authoring, 2026-07-27) rather than waiting on a not-yet-implemented dependency, unlike every `*TopologyRules` "designed ahead of a pending phase" precedent in this file (`SearchTopologyRules`, `IntelligenceTopologyRules`, `WorkflowTopologyRules`). Because this domain's own Test Rules forbid compiling real source files directly ("never test analyzers by compiling real source files manually" — `CSharpAnalyzerTest`/inline-markup only), the audit is executed as a manual/tool-assisted review: grep/read each domain's shipped `Result`/`Result<T>`-consuming call sites, catalog every DISTINCT real consumption shape encountered, then encode each shape as a representative (paraphrased, not literally copy-pasted) pass-path fixture — see T-266–T-269. If the audit finds a real call site structurally matching SK0030's fire condition, that is a genuine, previously-invisible defect in the OWNING domain's shipped code, not a false positive to "fix" by weakening the rule — record it as a new finding in T-270 and as a candidate follow-up work order in the owning domain, per this agent's jurisdiction boundary (`00.Governance` never implements another domain's production code).

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `Diagnostics/SK0030_ResultOutcomeDiscardedAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0030 — flags a bare-statement `Result`/`Result<T>` discard via the two-syntax-kind, outermost-type-only, `IHasSuccessFlag`-closure check |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/SK0030_ResultOutcomeDiscardedAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire-path tests (bare invocation, bare await, fluent-chain-still-a-Result) + pass-path tests (assignment, discard assignment, return, argument, void-terminal chain, non-Result baseline) + real-pattern audit fixtures modeled on 05.Application/06.Persistence/07.Messaging/17.Workflows's shipped consumption shapes |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | Diagnostic registry, implementation rules, changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] SK0030 fires on a bare-statement invocation of a method returning `Result` (non-generic) or `Result<T>`
- [ ] SK0030 fires on `await FooAsync();` as a bare statement where `FooAsync` returns `Task<Result<T>>` or `ValueTask<Result<T>>` — the documented edge case, with an explicit test
- [ ] SK0030 fires on a fluent-chain bare statement whose outermost call still resolves to an `IHasSuccessFlag`-implementing type (e.g. `Foo().Map(x => x + 1);`)
- [ ] SK0030 does NOT fire when the value is assigned to a variable or field (`var r = Foo();`, `result = Foo();`, `_field = Foo();`)
- [ ] SK0030 does NOT fire when the value is returned (`return Foo();`)
- [ ] SK0030 does NOT fire when the value is passed as an argument (`Bar(Foo());`)
- [ ] SK0030 does NOT fire when the value is the receiver of a member-access/method chain whose own outer type does not implement `IHasSuccessFlag` (`Foo().Match(onSuccess, onFailure);` where `Match` returns `void`)
- [ ] SK0030 does NOT fire on an explicit discard assignment (`_ = SomeMethodReturningResult();`)
- [ ] SK0030 does NOT fire on a bare-statement invocation of a method that does not implement `IHasSuccessFlag` (baseline sanity case)
- [ ] Diagnostic message explains the risk ("this Result's outcome is never checked — a failure will pass silently") and suggests the fix (assign, branch, return, pass as an argument, or explicitly discard with `_ =`)
- [ ] Analyzer test project includes both a violating fixture and a passing fixture for every consumption shape named in the phase input (assignment, return, argument, member-access receiver, awaited)
- [ ] **GATING, not deferred:** a real-source audit of `05.Application.Behaviors`, `06.Persistence.EfCore`, `07.Messaging.MassTransit`, and `17.Workflows.Temporal`'s shipped `Result`/`Result<T>`-consuming call sites is performed, every distinct real consumption shape found is encoded as a representative pass-path test fixture, and zero false positives are confirmed before this phase is considered complete — per this domain's Test Rules, via representative fixtures modeled on real shapes, never by compiling the real `.cs` files directly
- [ ] `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` documents SK0030 with a violating/compliant example pair, matching the existing SK0001–SK0029 documentation convention

### Dependencies

- Requires no other domain's future work. `05.Application`, `06.Persistence`, `07.Messaging`, and `17.Workflows` are all already Published as of this phase's authoring (2026-07-27) — the real-source audit reads their EXISTING shipped code; it does not wait on new work from any of them. No Cross-Domain Dependencies entry is added for this phase.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally — this is a terminal, self-contained enforcement rule. It does give every consuming domain a mechanical backstop against the exact class of silent-failure bug the platform's entire `Result<T>` design exists to prevent.

### Tooling Version Notes

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp`: 4.14.0 (existing pin — SK0030 reuses it, no version change)
- Target framework: `netstandard2.0` (`SharedKernel.Analyzers`)

## Phase SK.00.EfPropertyUsageGuard — Governance: Prohibit Raw EF.Property\<T\> Usage Outside Documented Exceptions <!-- phase-key: SK.00.EfPropertyUsageGuard -->

### Goal

WO-051 (P-327) mechanizes a "don't reintroduce this exact bug class" rule the platform has now had to fix TWICE by hand — first at P-105 (`EfReadRepository.GetByIdsAsync`), and again at P-316 (`TenantedRepository`'s two `GetByIdForTenantAsync*` methods) — proving that documenting the lesson in `06.Persistence/CLAUDE.md` after the first fix did not stop a second, independent occurrence of the identical "client-side evaluation via `EF.Property<TId>`" defect from shipping elsewhere in the same package. This phase adds a fourth predicate to the existing `EfCorePackageHygieneRules` class (introduced WO-017 P-103, home to the platform's other EfCore-package-scoped "prevent this exact regression" rules — `NoSpecificationEvaluatorDowncastInEfCoreAssembly` is the closest direct precedent), rather than a new platform-wide Roslyn analyzer: `EF.Property<TProperty>(object entity, string propertyName)` is a static method whose direct, executable-code invocation compiles to an ordinary `Call` IL opcode — but when the identical source-level call appears inside a lambda whose CONVERTED type is `Expression<TDelegate>` (the shape every legitimate use in this platform takes — a tenant/shadow-property `HasQueryFilter(Expression<Func<TEntity,bool>> filter)` global query filter), the C# compiler never emits that `Call` opcode at all: it lowers the entire lambda body into `System.Linq.Expressions.Expression`-builder calls instead, referencing `EF.Property<T>`'s `MethodInfo` only as metadata. A Mono.Cecil `Call`/`Callvirt` opcode-presence check therefore distinguishes the P-316 bug shape (direct, client-side-evaluated invocation) from the platform's one legitimate `EF.Property<T>` pattern automatically and for free — without needing to duplicate the compiler's own expression-tree-conversion determination inside a Roslyn analyzer's semantic-model logic, which the platform's other "prevent this exact regression" precedents (SK0013 raw-`HttpClient`, SK0020 ad hoc-logging) do not need to solve because neither has an analogous "same call, different compiled shape depending on context" ambiguity. No new SK diagnostic ID is assigned — this follows the `EfCorePackageHygieneRules` class's own established "EfCore-package-scoped regression-prevention rule, no SK ID" shape (all three of its existing predicates carry none), not the platform-wide Roslyn-analyzer shape the phase input's own motivating comparison cites.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoDirectEfPropertyUsagePredicate.cs`
  - Corresponding test file in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/EfCorePackageHygieneRules.cs` (new fourth method: `NoDirectEfPropertyUsageInEfCoreAssembly`); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. This phase adds a `NetArchTest` `ICustomRule` predicate to `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`, not a Roslyn analyzer — no new `SK` diagnostic ID is assigned. See Goal and Implementation Rules for the full rationale (mirrors the zero-SK-ID shape of this class's other three predicates, not the SK0013/SK0020 Roslyn-analyzer shape the phase input's own motivating comparison cites).

### Implementation Rules

1. `EfCorePackageHygieneRules.NoDirectEfPropertyUsageInEfCoreAssembly(Assembly)` → `ConditionList` is the fourth predicate in this class (after `NoSpecificationEvaluatorDowncastInEfCoreAssembly`, `IUnitOfWorkImplementorsMustHaveExactlyOneConstructor`, `ApplicationLayerMustNotReferenceDbContextTransaction`) and follows the class's established shape exactly: a single `Assembly` parameter, a `ConditionList` return, and an IL `Call`/`Callvirt` opcode-presence Mono.Cecil technique — the same technique already used by `NoDirectSaveChangesPredicate`/`NoMakeGenericMethodReflectionPredicate`/`NoTaskDelayOutsideResilienceBehaviorPredicate` — reused rather than reinvented.
2. `NoDirectEfPropertyUsagePredicate` matches `Call`/`Callvirt` IL opcodes whose operand `MethodReference.Name == "Property"` AND `MethodReference.DeclaringType.FullName == "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.EF"` — a `DeclaringType`+`Name` match, not a bare method-name match, following the same discriminator style `NoDbContextTransactionInApplicationPredicate`/`NoTaskDelayOutsideResilienceBehaviorPredicate` already use for BCL/framework static-method matches whose bare name alone could otherwise collide with an unrelated same-named member.
3. This rule carries NO exemption mechanism — no namespace guard, no allow-list registry (unlike `ReflectionExemptionRegistry`) — mirroring its immediate sibling `NoSpecificationEvaluatorDowncastInEfCoreAssembly`'s own zero-exemption precedent exactly. This is deliberate, not an oversight: the platform's one known legitimate `EF.Property<T>` pattern — a tenant/shadow-property global query filter built via `HasQueryFilter(Expression<Func<TEntity,bool>> filter)` — is structurally, automatically excluded without any exemption logic, because the C# compiler never emits a `Call`/`Callvirt` opcode targeting `EF.Property` when the call appears inside a lambda whose converted type is `Expression<TDelegate>`: the compiler instead lowers the entire lambda body into `System.Linq.Expressions.Expression`-builder calls, referencing `EF.Property<T>`'s `MethodInfo` only as metadata (via `ldtoken`/`GetMethodFromHandle`, or as an argument to an `Expression.Call(MethodInfo, ...)` overload) rather than invoking it directly. The predicate therefore only ever fires on a DIRECT, executable-code invocation of `EF.Property<T>` — exactly the client-side-evaluation defect class P-316 fixed — never on the idiomatic, EF-Core-blessed expression-tree usage. **This structural claim must be confirmed empirically during implementation** (compile the `HasQueryFilter`-shaped pass-path fixture, inspect the emitted IL directly) per this domain's established "confirmed empirically, not assumed" discipline (see SK0025's/`StorageTopologyRules`'/`SearchTopologyRules`'s own precedent) — do not simply trust this design note as given.
4. If a genuinely justified DIRECT (non-expression-tree) `EF.Property<T>` usage is ever found in `SharedKernel.Persistence.EfCore` in the future, it requires a governance review and an explicit, documented revision of this entry — adding an exemption mechanism (e.g., a small allow-list registry mirroring `ReflectionExemptionRegistry`'s shape) — before any suppression is applied in code. There is no `#pragma`-style suppression for `ICustomRule`-backed `NetArchTest` violations; the only sanctioned remediation paths are (a) refactor to the `Expression.Property` pattern, or (b) a governance-reviewed registry addition recorded here first.
5. This phase introduces zero new SK diagnostic IDs and zero new NuGet dependency — reuses the existing `Mono.Cecil >= 0.11.5` reference already in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`. `EfCorePackageHygieneRules`'s three existing predicates carry no SK ID either; this fourth predicate follows that same "EfCore-package-scoped regression-prevention rule, no SK ID" shape rather than the platform-wide "raw-`HttpClient` (SK0013) / ad hoc-logging (SK0020)" Roslyn-analyzer shape the phase input's own motivating comparison cites — a deliberate design decision by this domain's own architect: the IL-opcode-presence technique naturally distinguishes direct-call misuse from expression-tree-embedded correct usage without needing to duplicate the C# compiler's own expression-tree-conversion determination inside a Roslyn analyzer's semantic-model logic (which would otherwise require checking `SemanticModel.GetTypeInfo(enclosingLambda).ConvertedType` against `Expression<TDelegate>`).
6. Real-assembly status: UNVERIFIABLE / GATING as of this phase's authoring (2026-07-30) — `06.Persistence`'s own P-316 (migrate `TenantedRepository`'s two `GetByIdForTenantAsync*` methods off `EF.Property<TId>` to the `Expression.Property` pattern) is planned in `06.Persistence/state-map.md` but not yet implemented; the offending `EF.Property<TId>` call sites are still live in the shipped source as of this phase's authoring. Design, implementation, and initial tests proceed now against CONTRIVED in-memory Mono.Cecil fixtures only; the real-assembly re-verification pass against the corrected `SharedKernel.Persistence.EfCore` assembly is a GATING acceptance criterion, not a non-blocking follow-up, mirroring the `SK.00.SearchTopology`/`SK.00.IntelligenceTopology`/`SK.00.WorkflowTopology` precedent — it must be completed, with its own acceptance-criterion checkbox explicitly closed, before this phase can be marked fully `●` complete.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `Predicates/NoDirectEfPropertyUsagePredicate.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | `ICustomRule` — flags a `Call`/`Callvirt` IL opcode targeting `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.EF::Property` found via direct executable-code invocation (structurally excludes expression-tree-embedded usage) |
| `Rules/EfCorePackageHygieneRules.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Modify | Add fourth method `NoDirectEfPropertyUsageInEfCoreAssembly(Assembly)` → `ConditionList` |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/EfCorePackageHygieneRulesTests.cs` (or equivalent) | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify | Fire-path tests (direct call in ordinary method body; direct call inside a non-expression-tree `Func<T,bool>` lambda) + pass-path tests (no `EF.Property` usage at all, modeled on the P-316-corrected `Expression.Property` pattern; `EF.Property` used inside a `HasQueryFilter`-shaped `Expression<Func<T,bool>>` lambda — the structural self-exemption proof) |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | Architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `NoDirectEfPropertyUsageInEfCoreAssembly` fires when `EF.Property<T>(...)` is called directly in ordinary (non-expression-tree) executable code inside the supplied assembly — reproducing the exact pattern P-316 fixed
- [ ] The rule fires when `EF.Property<T>(...)` is called inside a lambda passed as `Func<T,bool>` (a non-expression-tree, client-side-evaluated delegate) — proving detection is not merely "outside any lambda"
- [ ] The rule does NOT fire against a fixture using the P-316-corrected `Expression.Property`-based pattern (no `EF.Property` call present at all)
- [ ] The rule does NOT fire when `EF.Property<T>(...)` is used inside a lambda whose converted type is `Expression<Func<T,bool>>` (a `HasQueryFilter`-shaped global query filter) — the structural self-exemption for the platform's one legitimate usage, confirmed empirically against real compiled IL during implementation, not merely assumed from this design's prose
- [ ] **GATING, not deferred:** the rule is re-pointed at the real, corrected `SharedKernel.Persistence.EfCore` assembly (post-P-316) and confirmed to report zero violations — this cannot be satisfied until 06.Persistence's P-316 ships; the implementer must sequence this phase's own implementation after P-316 lands, per the dispatcher's own explicit note
- [ ] `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` documents the rule with the P-316 defect (and its P-105 precedent) as the motivating example, mirroring the documentation style of the platform's other "prevent this exact regression" rules (`NoSpecificationEvaluatorDowncastInEfCoreAssembly`, SK0013, SK0020)

### Dependencies

- Requires `06.Persistence` P-316 (`TenantedRepository`'s two `GetByIdForTenantAsync*` methods migrated off `EF.Property<TId>` to `Expression.Property`) before the real-assembly verification acceptance criterion can be satisfied. Design, implementation, and the four contrived-fixture tests may proceed now; the GATING real-assembly check is deferred until P-316 ships — mirroring the `SK.00.SearchTopology`/`SK.00.IntelligenceTopology`/`SK.00.WorkflowTopology` precedent, but for a persistence-layer dependency rather than a not-yet-built domain.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally — a terminal, self-contained regression-prevention rule. It does close the mechanical gap that let the identical P-105 defect class recur once already (at P-316) with no build-time signal.

### Tooling Version Notes

- `NetArchTest.eNt`: existing pin (no version change)
- `Mono.Cecil`: `>= 0.11.5` (existing pin — reused, no new dependency)
- Target framework: `net10.0` (`SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`)

## Phase SK.00.EventEnvelopeConstructionGuard — Governance: Prohibit Direct EventEnvelope Construction Outside Its Mandated Factory <!-- phase-key: SK.00.EventEnvelopeConstructionGuard -->

### Goal

WO-054's messaging-domain review (P-340, dispatched by `messaging-arch-planner` earlier in this same run) found the platform's own shipped `MassTransitEventPublisher.PublishEnvelope<TEvent>` (`07.Messaging/SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit`) constructing `04.Contracts`'s `EventEnvelope<TEvent>` — the platform's single cross-service event wire format — via a raw object initializer instead of the type's own, XML-doc-mandated `EventEnvelope.Wrap<TEvent>()` factory, silently dropping the `TenantId` field `04.Contracts` shipped specifically for cross-service tenant routing (WO-052/P-331). This phase mechanizes that documented-but-unenforced construction-path contract the same way the platform closed every prior "one correct construction path" gap — raw `HttpClient` (SK0013), ad hoc logging (SK0020/21), inline `ProblemDetails` (`PresentationLayeringRules`, WO-031 P-199) — so it cannot silently regress again, in `07.Messaging` or any future consumer of `EventEnvelope<TEvent>`.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoDirectEventEnvelopeConstructionPredicate.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/ContractsLayeringRules.cs` (new class)
  - Corresponding test file(s) in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to the real `SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit` assembly — needed immediately for T-279, not deferred, since the CURRENT pre-P-340 assembly already contains the exact violation this phase exists to catch); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. This phase adds a `NetArchTest` `ICustomRule` predicate to `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`, not a Roslyn analyzer — no new `SK` diagnostic ID is assigned. `PresentationLayeringRules.NoDirectProblemDetailsConstructionOutsideWebApi` (a sealed wire-format type with exactly one legitimate construction site, detected via `Newobj` IL-opcode presence, caller-controlled package exclusion) is the closer structural analog than the phase input's own cited SK0013/SK0020 Roslyn-analyzer precedents, and the phase input's own acceptance criterion — verification against "real compiled assemblies" — is this domain's established idiom for the IL/Mono.Cecil technique. See Implementation Rules for the full rationale.

### Implementation Rules

1. `ContractsLayeringRules.NoDirectEventEnvelopeConstructionOutsideContracts(params Assembly[] assemblies)` → `ConditionList` is a NEW static class (not a fifth predicate on the existing `ContractsPurityRules`) — `ContractsPurityRules` governs `04.Contracts`'s OWN internal purity (no domain types on its public surface, no non-trivial methods, sealed integration events); this rule governs how OTHER assemblies must construct one of `04.Contracts`'s types, the same "protect this domain's boundary from outside misuse" direction `PresentationLayeringRules`/`CommunicationLayeringRules`/`MessagingArchitectureRules` already established under a `{Domain}LayeringRules` name.
2. `NoDirectEventEnvelopeConstructionPredicate` matches a `Newobj` IL opcode on THREE conditions, all of which must hold: `MethodReference.DeclaringType.Namespace == "SharedKernel.Contracts.Events"`, `MethodReference.DeclaringType.Name` equal to `EventEnvelope`'s generic-arity-suffixed simple name (Mono.Cecil's undecorated simple-name shape for a generic type — the same technique family as `NoDirectEncryptedValueConverterInstantiationPredicate`'s `.Name.Contains(...)` match, refined to an exact Namespace+Name pair since "EventEnvelope" alone is a more collision-prone simple name than "EncryptedValueConverter"), and `MethodReference.Parameters.Count == 0`.
3. The `Parameters.Count == 0` condition is this domain's FIRST constructor-arity discriminator on a generic-`Newobj` predicate — every prior generic-`Newobj` predicate in this domain (`NoDirectEncryptedValueConverterInstantiationPredicate`, `NoDirectProblemDetailsConstructionPredicate`) matches on `DeclaringType` alone because none of their target types carries a second, differently-shaped legitimate constructor to avoid flagging. `EventEnvelope<TEvent>` (a `sealed record` with only `required ... { get; init; }` properties and no positional parameter list) synthesizes a public PARAMETERLESS constructor (used by `new EventEnvelope<TEvent> { ... }` object-initializer syntax — this rule's fire condition) AND a separate ONE-parameter copy constructor (used by `with` expressions on an already-`Wrap`-constructed instance — deliberately excluded, since a `with` expression mutates an existing legitimately-constructed envelope rather than fabricating new envelope identity/routing metadata from scratch).
4. No exemption mechanism inside the predicate — mirrors `PresentationLayeringRules`'s caller-controlled-exclusion convention exactly: the caller never passes `SharedKernel.Contracts` to the factory method. A caller that legitimately invokes `EventEnvelope.Wrap<TEvent>()` needs no exemption at all — its own compiled IL contains only a `Call`/`Callvirt` to `EventEnvelope.Wrap`, never a `Newobj` targeting `EventEnvelope<TEvent>`; the `newobj` instruction that actually constructs the record lives inside `SharedKernel.Contracts.dll`'s own `Wrap<TEvent>` method body, a different assembly entirely. This is a structural (cross-assembly IL locality), not policy-based, non-detection.
5. Real-assembly status is SPLIT, unlike every prior `*TopologyRules`/`*PackageHygiene` GATING precedent in this file: the FIRE-path check against the CURRENT, not-yet-corrected real `SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit` assembly is NON-GATING and can (and should) run immediately — as of this phase's authoring, `07.Messaging`'s own P-340 (`SK.07.EnvelopeTenancy`, ET-04) is planned but not yet implemented, so `MassTransitEventPublisher.PublishEnvelope<TEvent>` still contains the exact raw object-initializer violation this phase exists to catch (T-279). The PASS-path check against the corrected assembly IS GATING on `07.Messaging` P-340 shipping (T-280) — mirroring the `SK.00.EfPropertyUsageGuard`/`SK.00.SearchTopology`/`SK.00.IntelligenceTopology`/`SK.00.WorkflowTopology` precedent for a not-yet-implemented dependency, but for the first time in this file, one half of the real-assembly proof does not need to wait.
6. Zero new SK diagnostic ID, zero new Mono.Cecil technique beyond the constructor-arity refinement (item 3), zero new NuGet dependency — reuses the existing `Mono.Cecil >= 0.11.5` reference already in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `Predicates/NoDirectEventEnvelopeConstructionPredicate.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | `ICustomRule` — flags a `Newobj` IL opcode targeting `EventEnvelope<TEvent>`'s parameterless constructor |
| `Rules/ContractsLayeringRules.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | New static class; single method `NoDirectEventEnvelopeConstructionOutsideContracts(params Assembly[])` → `ConditionList` |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/ContractsLayeringRulesTests.cs` (or equivalent) | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Create | Fire-path (contrived + real pre-fix) and pass-path (contrived Wrap-call, contrived `with`-expression, contrived no-usage, real post-fix GATING) tests |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify | Test-only `ProjectReference` (`PrivateAssets="all"`) to `SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit`, needed immediately for T-279 |

- [x] The rule does NOT fire against a fixture that legitimately calls `EventEnvelope.Wrap<TEvent>()` — confirm empirically that no `Newobj` targeting `EventEnvelope<TEvent>` appears in the caller's own compiled IL (T-276)
- [x] The rule does NOT fire against a fixture using a `with` expression on an already-`Wrap`-constructed envelope — confirm empirically that the copy constructor's parameter count (1) is structurally distinct from the fire condition's parameter count (0) (T-277)
- [x] The rule does NOT fire against a fixture with zero `EventEnvelope` usage (T-278)
- [x] **SUPERSEDED (verified 2026-08-07):** originally "NON-GATING, run immediately: the rule fires against the REAL, CURRENT `SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit` assembly, reproducing `MassTransitEventPublisher.PublishEnvelope<TEvent>`'s actual shipped violation." `07.Messaging` P-340 shipped 2026-08-05, before this criterion was checked — the real assembly no longer contains the violation, so there is nothing to fire against. Not force-failed; the contrived fixture T-275 is the primary red proof instead (T-279)
- [x] **GATING, satisfied 2026-08-07 (not deferred):** the rule is re-pointed at the real, POST-P-340-corrected `SharedKernel.Messaging.MassTransit` assembly and confirmed to report zero violations — `07.Messaging`'s P-340 (`SK.07.EnvelopeTenancy`, ET-04) shipped 2026-08-05; `ContractsLayeringRulesTests.NoDirectEventEnvelopeConstructionOutsideContracts_RealMassTransitAssembly_RulePasses` confirms zero violations against the real assembly (T-280)

### Dependencies

Design, implementation, all four contrived-fixture tests, AND the real-assembly FIRE-path test against the current, uncorrected assembly (T-279) may all proceed now — P-340 blocks only the final pass-path re-verification.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally — a terminal, self-contained regression-prevention rule. It does close the platform's one shipped, documented-but-unenforced wire-format construction-path gap this review's own findings surfaced, before it becomes the first of several such violations rather than the only one.

## Phase SK.00.SecurityContextGuard — Governance: Mechanically Enforce 12.Security's Documented Hard Rules <!-- phase-key: SK.00.SecurityContextGuard -->

### Goal

`12.Security/CLAUDE.md` has documented three hard rules since its original build-out (SK.12.Core, 2026-06-02) and never mechanized any of them: (1) `03.Domain` types must never reference `ITenantProvider`; (2) application/domain-adjacent code must inject `IUserContext`/`ITenantProvider` — never `IHttpContextAccessor`, `ClaimsPrincipal`, or `HttpContext` directly; (3) `IUserContext`/`ITenantProvider` must never be registered as a singleton. This phase mechanizes all three the same way the platform has repeatedly closed this exact class of gap — raw `HttpClient` (SK0013, P-159), inline `ProblemDetails` construction (`PresentationLayeringRules`, P-199), ad hoc logging (SK0020/21, P-250), direct `EventEnvelope` construction (`ContractsLayeringRules`, P-350), and discarded `Result` outcomes (SK0030, P-299) are all the identical shape of fix applied to a different domain. `12.Security` is the one domain carrying three explicitly documented hard rules — a layering rule, a construction-path rule, and a DI-lifetime rule — with zero governance coverage of any of them, despite the domain's own brain stating plainly that violating them (a `03.Domain` type coupling to tenant context, or `IUserContext`/`ITenantProvider` accidentally captured as a singleton and leaking identity/tenant context across requests) is a serious correctness/security defect, not a style violation. This is the platform's first `12.Security`-domain governance phase.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/SK0031_RawSecurityContextConstructorInjectionAnalyzer.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/SK0031_RawSecurityContextConstructorInjectionAnalyzerTests.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoTenantProviderReferenceInDomainPredicate.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/SecurityArchitectureRules.cs` (new class)
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecurityArchitectureRulesTests.cs`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (test-only `ProjectReference`s, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Domain` and `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc`, if not already present); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0031 | RawSecurityContextConstructorInjection | Usage | Warning | Constructor injection of `IHttpContextAccessor`/`ClaimsPrincipal`/`HttpContext` outside `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc`/`SharedKernel.Security.ApiKey` |

### Implementation Rules

1. `RawSecurityContextConstructorInjectionAnalyzer` (SK0031) is syntax-only — no `SemanticModel` required — mirroring SK0013's exact `ConstructorDeclarationSyntax`-parameter simple-name-match shape and `SyntaxNode.Parent` namespace-ancestor exemption walk.
2. SK0031's exemption covers TWO namespace prefixes, not one: `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` (the real, shipped implementation package that legitimately constructs `OidcUserContext`/`OidcTenantProvider` from `IHttpContextAccessor`) and `SharedKernel.Security.ApiKey` (named verbatim in this phase's own input; no such package exists in the platform as of this phase — `12.Security` ships only `.Abstractions` and `.Oidc`). Include it as a forward-looking, currently-vacuous exemption; revise it in the same PR if a future API-key provider package ships under a different name.
3. `SecurityArchitectureRules.DomainNeverReferencesTenantProvider(Assembly domainAssembly)` → `ConditionList` is backed by `NoTenantProviderReferenceInDomainPredicate`, which reuses `NoDbContextTransactionInApplicationPredicate`'s established three-surface (fields, constructor/method parameters, instruction-operand types) inspection technique against an exact-`FullName` match on `SharedKernel.Security.Abstractions.ITenantProvider`. No exemption — 03.Domain must never reference it under any circumstance.
4. `SecurityArchitectureRules.NoSingletonRegistrationOfSecurityContextTypes(params Assembly[] assemblies)` → `ConditionList` is backed by `NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate`, which introduces this domain's newest Mono.Cecil technique — generic-instance-method-argument inspection (`GenericInstanceMethod.GenericArguments` on a resolved `AddSingleton` call) — because this phase's own acceptance criteria explicitly call for an architecture-test rule, not an analyzer, for the singleton-lifetime check (unlike SK0703/SK0023, which are Roslyn analyzers for their respective misregistration classes). No exemption — `IUserContext`/`ITenantProvider` must never be singleton anywhere.
5. `NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate` carries one documented limitation: it detects only the closed-generic `AddSingleton<TService>(...)`/`AddSingleton<TService,TImpl>(...)` call shapes, not the non-generic `AddSingleton(Type, Type)`/`AddSingleton(Type, Func<...>)` overloads — mirroring `HealthCheckTagIntegrityRules`'s own documented data-flow limitation.
6. Zero new SK ID for either `SecurityArchitectureRules` method — follows the `EfCorePackageHygieneRules`/`RedisTopologyRules` "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention. Both reuse the existing `Mono.Cecil >= 0.11.5` reference already in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` — zero new NuGet dependency.
7. Real-assembly verification for all three rules is NON-GATING and immediately available — unlike most recent phases in this file, both `12.Security` (`.Abstractions`/`.Oidc`) and `03.Domain` are already fully Published as of this phase's authoring (`12.Security/CLAUDE.md`'s own changelog records `SK.12.Published complete`, 2026-06-02; `03.Domain` shipped `SharedKernel.Domain` v1.7.0 at WO-051). The implementer should wire real-assembly tests directly, not defer them as a follow-up.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A NetArchTest rule (`SecurityArchitectureRules.DomainNeverReferencesTenantProvider`) fails the build if any type in `03.Domain` references `SharedKernel.Security.Abstractions.ITenantProvider`

## Phase SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard — Governance: Mechanize Sender-Constrained-Token and mTLS-Certificate-Validation Locality Rules <!-- phase-key: SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard -->

### Goal

`SK.00.SecurityContextGuard` (P-373) established the pattern this phase repeats: `12.Security` hard rules documented in prose accumulate silent violations if nothing mechanizes them — that phase closed three such gaps that had gone unenforced since the domain's original build-out. `12.Security` is about to gain two new sender-constraining credential mechanisms — DPoP proof validation (`P-376`, extending `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc`) and mTLS client-certificate validation (`P-377`, a new `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` sibling provider package) — both dispatched to `security-arch-planner` in the same run as this phase but not yet implemented. This phase extends the existing `SecurityArchitectureRules` static class (not a new class — both new rules are the same "protect this domain's hard rules mechanically" shape as `SecurityContextGuard`'s own two methods) with two more locality predicates, applying the P-373 lesson proactively instead of retroactively: mechanize the "this validation logic lives in exactly one package" rule at design time, before either new provider ships, rather than waiting for a future gold-standard review to discover the drift.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` only — no `SharedKernel.Analyzers` change, per this phase's own acceptance criteria, which call for architecture-test predicates (not Roslyn analyzers) for both rules.
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoDpopProofValidationDuplicationPredicate.cs`
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoRawClientCertificateAccessOutsideMtlsPredicate.cs`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/SecurityArchitectureRules.cs` (two new methods added to the EXISTING class from P-373 — not a new class); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecurityArchitectureRulesTests.cs` (new contrived fire/pass-path tests); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (test-only `ProjectReference`s, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` — already present since P-373 — and, once it exists on disk, `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls`); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. Both new rules are `NetArchTest` `ICustomRule` predicates added to the existing `SecurityArchitectureRules` class, not Roslyn analyzers — no new `SK` diagnostic ID is assigned, following the exact same "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention `SecurityArchitectureRules`'s own first two methods (`DomainNeverReferencesTenantProvider`, `NoSingletonRegistrationOfSecurityContextTypes`, both P-373) already established, and consistent with `EfCorePackageHygieneRules`/`RedisTopologyRules`. SK0032 remains the next available sequential ID for a future genuine Roslyn analyzer — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. `SecurityArchitectureRules.DpopProofValidationNeverDuplicatedOutsideOidc(params Assembly[] assemblies)` → `ConditionList` is backed by `NoDpopProofValidationDuplicationPredicate`, which checks TWO independent surfaces inside every method body, mirroring the "multiple detection surfaces feeding one predicate" shape already used by `NoTenantProviderReferenceInDomainPredicate` (P-373): (a) an `Ldstr` IL instruction whose operand is exactly `"DPoP"` (case-sensitive, the RFC 9449 canonical header name) — reusing the Ldstr literal-collection technique already established by `HealthCheckTagIntegrityRules`/`MetricsInstrumentationRules`; (b) a `Call`/`Callvirt`/`Newobj` instruction whose resolved operand's declaring type `FullName` is exactly `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt.JwtSecurityTokenHandler` or `Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens.JsonWebTokenHandler` — reusing SK0301's (`NoAesCipherInDomainOrApplicationPredicate`) raw-type-reference technique, applied to JWT-proof-parsing types instead of cipher types. Either surface matching outside the exempted namespace violates the rule.
2. Exemption: `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` only — the real, shipped (once `P-376` lands) DPoP-proof-validation implementation package. No `SharedKernel.Security.ApiKey`-style second forward-looking exemption prefix here — DPoP is exclusively an OIDC/JWT-bearer-adjacent concern, unlike SK0031's raw-`HttpContext`-family check, which spans every identity provider package.
3. `SecurityArchitectureRules.ClientCertificateAccessNeverDuplicatedOutsideMtls(params Assembly[] assemblies)` → `ConditionList` is backed by `NoRawClientCertificateAccessOutsideMtlsPredicate`, a single-surface IL match: a `Call`/`Callvirt` instruction whose resolved `MethodReference.Name == "get_ClientCertificate"` and `MethodReference.DeclaringType.FullName == "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.ConnectionInfo"` — the property-getter shape of `HttpContext.Connection.ClientCertificate`. This single, precise signal satisfies both halves of the acceptance criterion's "`HttpContext.Connection.ClientCertificate`/`X509Certificate2`" phrasing in one match, since `ConnectionInfo.ClientCertificate` IS declared as `X509Certificate2?` — a bare "any `X509Certificate2` type reference" surface was deliberately rejected as a second condition because `01.Core/SharedKernel.Cryptography`'s `IAsymmetricSignatureService` legitimately handles X.509-adjacent cryptographic material for unrelated (non-HTTP-connection) signing/verification purposes, and a broad type-reference match would false-positive there.
4. Exemption: `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` only — the new sibling provider package `P-377` will ship.
5. Zero new SK ID for either method — see Diagnostic Registry Changes. Both reuse the existing `Mono.Cecil >= 0.11.5` reference already in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` — zero new NuGet dependency.
6. Real-assembly verification for BOTH rules is UNVERIFIABLE/non-gating on THIS phase's own completion, per this phase's own explicit acceptance criterion — dispatched deliberately last in WO-058's dependency order because `P-376`/`P-377` were dispatched to `security-arch-planner` in the same run and are planned but NOT YET IMPLEMENTED; neither `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc`'s DPoP surface nor `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` exists on disk today. Design, implementation, and all contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests may proceed now; the GATING real-assembly re-verification is tracked as a Cross-Domain Dependency and completed in a follow-up pass once both upstream phases ship — mirroring the `SK.00.MagicStringGuard`/`SK.00.EfPropertyUsageGuard` precedent for a not-yet-implemented dependency, not the `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`/`SK.00.EventEnvelopeConstructionGuard` precedent where the target assembly (or an uncorrected predecessor of it) already existed at authoring time.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `Predicates/NoDpopProofValidationDuplicationPredicate.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | `ICustomRule` — flags a raw `"DPoP"` Ldstr literal or a JWT-proof-parsing type reference (`JwtSecurityTokenHandler`/`JsonWebTokenHandler`) outside `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` |
| `Predicates/NoRawClientCertificateAccessOutsideMtlsPredicate.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | `ICustomRule` — flags a `ConnectionInfo.ClientCertificate` property-getter call outside `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` |
| `Rules/SecurityArchitectureRules.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Modify | Two new methods added to the existing class (from P-373): `DpopProofValidationNeverDuplicatedOutsideOidc`, `ClientCertificateAccessNeverDuplicatedOutsideMtls` |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecurityArchitectureRulesTests.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify | New contrived fire/pass-path tests for both rules; real-assembly tests added in a follow-up pass once `P-376`/`P-377` ship |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify (deferred) | Test-only `ProjectReference` (`PrivateAssets="all"`) to `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls`, added once that package exists on disk |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | Architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SecurityArchitectureRules.DpopProofValidationNeverDuplicatedOutsideOidc` fails the build if any type outside `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` references the `"DPoP"` header-name literal or a JWT-proof-parsing type (`JwtSecurityTokenHandler`/`JsonWebTokenHandler`) — proven now against contrived fixtures

- [ ] Both rules are proven against the real, compiled `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc`/`SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` assemblies once `P-376`/`P-377` ship — NON-GATING on this phase's own completion, tracked as a Cross-Domain Dependency, not deferred silently
- [ ] `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`'s Diagnostic Rule Registry (no change — no new SK ID) and Architecture Test Contracts sections are updated alongside the existing `SecurityArchitectureRules`/P-373 entries

### Dependencies

- Requires: none for design/implementation/contrived tests — proceeds immediately. Requires `12.Security` `P-376` (DPoP) and `P-377` (`SharedKernel.Security.Mtls`) before the two real-assembly re-verification tests can be written — tracked below under Cross-Domain Dependencies.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally — a terminal, self-contained regression-prevention rule set, mirroring `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`'s own "close it before it becomes the first of several such violations" motivation, applied here before either violation has ever shipped.

## Phase SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock — Governance: Mechanically Lock Secure-by-Default JWT/mTLS Validation Configuration <!-- phase-key: SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock -->

### Goal

Two configuration defects found during the WO-060 fintech/FAPI-grade review (P-385, P-386) both happened silently inside already-reviewed, already-tested, already-published `12.Security` code from a session explicitly scoped as a "fintech/FAPI 2.0-grade" hardening pass: `MtlsAuthenticationOptions` shipped with `AllowedCertificateTypes = CertificateTypes.All`/`RevocationMode = X509RevocationMode.NoCheck` — WEAKER than plain ASP.NET Core's own `CertificateAuthenticationOptions` default — and nothing asserted the corrected default values themselves once P-386 fixed them. This phase mechanizes those corrected defaults (and the new P-387 JWS signing-algorithm allowlist) the same way `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard` (P-373) mechanized `12.Security`'s three original hard rules: a security-relevant convention documented only in prose eventually drifts, and a future edit to `MtlsAuthenticationOptions` or the JWT Bearer/DPoP configuration could reintroduce a weaker default with every existing test still green unless the default VALUES themselves are asserted, not merely the code shape around them.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` only — no `SharedKernel.Analyzers` change. This is a default-VALUE check (what a default-constructed options instance's properties actually resolve to), not a call-site code-pattern check — the shape neither a Roslyn analyzer (no source-level anti-pattern to flag; the shipped code that set `CertificateTypes.All` was syntactically unremarkable) nor a `ConditionList` assembly-dependency check (no forbidden namespace reference is involved) naturally expresses. It is the same class of concern as `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`/`WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` — a plain public helper, not `ConditionList`/`ICustomRule`.
- New files:
  - `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/SecureDefaultsAssertion.cs`
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (new, contrived fixture fire/pass-path tests now; real-assembly tests added in a follow-up pass once `P-386`/`P-387` ship); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (test-only `ProjectReference`s, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` and `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` — `.Oidc` already present since `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`/P-373 — added once each package's corrected defaults exist on disk); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. Both new checks are plain public-helper assertions over Mono.Cecil-resolved default property values — not Roslyn analyzers, not `NetArchTest`/`ICustomRule` predicates. No new `SK` diagnostic ID is assigned, following the same "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention `SecurityArchitectureRules`'s methods and `SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`'s two new methods already established. SK0032 remains the next available sequential ID for a future genuine Roslyn analyzer — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. `SecureDefaultsAssertion` is the domain's FOURTH non-`ConditionList`/`ICustomRule` public helper, after `ApplicationPipelineRules.PipelineOrderAssertion`, `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`, and `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion` — same rationale: "a specific type's specific property resolves to a specific default value" has no single-assembly "fire on a contrived violating assembly" shape a `ConditionList` naturally expresses, and no source-level anti-pattern a Roslyn analyzer could target (the P-385/P-386 defect was a correctly-shaped, syntactically unremarkable property initializer with the wrong constant).
2. `.AssertEnumPropertyDefaultEquals(Type optionsType, string propertyName, string expectedEnumMemberName)` introduces this domain's NEWEST Mono.Cecil technique — **constructor/property-initializer enum-default-value resolution**. Loads `optionsType`'s `TypeDefinition` via Mono.Cecil, locates its parameterless instance constructor (`IsConstructor && Parameters.Count == 0` — Roslyn emits property-initializer assignments at the start of every constructor body, in declaration order, before any explicit constructor logic), finds the `Stfld` targeting `propertyName`'s compiler-generated backing field (`<propertyName>k__BackingField`), reads the immediately-preceding `Ldc_I4`-family opcode's loaded integral constant, and resolves the enum member name by matching that constant against the property's enum type's own `Fields` (excluding the special `value__` field) `Constant` values. Compares the resolved member name (case-sensitive) against `expectedEnumMemberName`. This is a DIFFERENT technique from `StringConstantsClassDetector`'s field-shape+literal-value resolution (which resolves `const`/`static readonly string` FIELDS directly) — here the value is resolved from a property AUTO-INITIALIZER assigned inside a constructor body, and the value type is an enum's underlying integral constant, not a string.
3. `.AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultExcludes(Type optionsType, string propertyName, IReadOnlyCollection<string> forbiddenValues, bool requireNonEmpty = true)` extends the established `Ldstr` literal-collection technique (`HealthCheckTagIntegrityRules`/`MetricsInstrumentationRules`) to a NEW call-site shape — a constructor-body array/collection-initializer feeding a property's backing-field `Stfld`, rather than a method-name-prefix-scoped call site. Collects every `Ldstr` operand appearing in the initializer sequence immediately preceding the `Stfld` targeting `propertyName`'s backing field. Fails if the collected set is empty (covers BOTH a `null` default, which produces zero collected literals since no array/collection-initializer IL exists at all, AND an explicit empty-array default, `Array.Empty<string>()`/`new string[0]`, which produces zero `Ldstr` operands — both shapes satisfy the acceptance criterion's "empty, null" wording via the same one non-empty check) unless `requireNonEmpty: false`. Fails if the collected set's intersection with `forbiddenValues` (case-insensitive comparison — JWS `alg` values are compared case-insensitively here defensively, even though RFC 7518 defines `"none"` as lowercase-exact, since this check validates a HARDENED DEFAULT rather than parsing untrusted wire input) is non-empty.
4. Both methods throw a single test-framework-agnostic assertion exception naming the property, the actual resolved default, and the expected/forbidden value(s) on failure — the same aggregate-failure-message convention as `PipelineOrderAssertion`/`LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`/`WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion`.
5. Caller-supplied everything: `00.Governance` never references `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls`/`.Oidc` directly (`00.Governance` references nothing). The consuming test project supplies `optionsType` via `typeof(MtlsAuthenticationOptions)`/the real JWT sub-options type/`DpopOptions` (test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`), `expectedEnumMemberName`/`forbiddenValues` from the real, shipped hardened-default values once `P-386`/`P-387` land — matching the same "caller supplies the assembly/values, never hard-code them here" discipline established by every prior non-`ConditionList` helper in this file.
6. Real-assembly verification for BOTH checks is UNVERIFIABLE/non-gating on THIS phase's own completion, mirroring `SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`'s own precedent exactly (dispatched in the same WO-060 run, both `P-386`/`P-387` are `○ QUEUED` — design-locked but not yet dispatched for implementation — as of this phase's authoring). Design, implementation, and all contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests proceed now; the GATING real-assembly re-verification is tracked as a Cross-Domain Dependency and completed in a follow-up pass once both upstream phases ship.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `SecureDefaultsAssertion.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | Public helper — `AssertEnumPropertyDefaultEquals`, `AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultExcludes` |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Create | Contrived fixture fire/pass-path tests for both methods; real-assembly tests added once `P-386`/`P-387` ship |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify (deferred) | Test-only `ProjectReference`s (`PrivateAssets="all"`) to `SharedKernel.Security.Mtls` (new) and `SharedKernel.Security.Oidc` (already present) once each package's corrected defaults exist on disk |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | Architecture test contracts, implementation rules, changelog (already applied) |

Verified false at implementation time — `12.Security` had already shipped its full WO-060 scope (C-39/C-40/C-41 all `●` Complete) before this phase's implementation session began, mirroring `SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`'s own immediately-preceding closeout correction in the same WO-060 run. ## Phase SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock — Governance: Mechanically Lock the Corrected Tenant-Resolution and mTLS Trust-Boundary Defaults <!-- phase-key: SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock -->

### Goal

`13.ServiceDefaults`'s WO-061 gold-standard/big-fintech review (dispatched to `servicedefaults-arch-planner` immediately before this phase) found two security-relevant defaults that, left undocumented-only, would silently regress: `TenantResolutionOptions.StrategyOrder`'s default `[Header, Claim, Database]` order let an unsigned, caller-supplied `X-Tenant-Id` header outrank a cryptographically-verified JWT tenant claim for the same request (the exact cross-tenant-impersonation shape P-393's corrected `[Claim, Header, Database]` order closes), and `MtlsForwardedHeaderMiddleware`'s unconfigured-`TrustedNetworks` posture relies entirely on a startup `Warning` log statement (P-394/P-395's `ServiceDefaultsLog.ForwardedHeaderTrustBoundaryUnconfigured`) to signal that any network path reaching the host directly can forge a client-certificate header — a warning a future edit could delete with every existing test still green. This is the THIRD time in this review cycle the identical bug class has surfaced — `12.Security`'s WO-060 pass found it twice (`MtlsAuthenticationOptions`'s weaker-than-framework-default `AllowedCertificateTypes`/`RevocationMode`, mechanized by `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390) — and this phase applies the now-established `SecureDefaultsAssertion` pattern to `13.ServiceDefaults` for the first time: a hardened default or a security-relevant log statement documented only in prose is not durable; it must be asserted against the real, compiled default-constructed instance/method body, the same way `SecureDefaultsAssertion.AssertEnumPropertyDefaultEquals`/`.AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultExcludes` already lock `12.Security`'s corrected defaults in place.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` only — no `SharedKernel.Analyzers` change. Both new checks are default-VALUE and call-site-PRESENCE checks over Mono.Cecil-resolved IL, the same class of concern `SecureDefaultsAssertion`'s existing two methods already address — no source-level anti-pattern for a Roslyn analyzer to target, no single-assembly dependency shape a `ConditionList` naturally expresses.
- New files: none — both checks extend the EXISTING `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class from `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390, not a new class, mirroring the `SecurityArchitectureRules`-extension precedent (`SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard` added two methods to `SecurityArchitectureRules` rather than opening a new class).
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/SecureDefaultsAssertion.cs` (two new methods); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (new contrived fixture fire/pass-path tests now; real-assembly tests added once `P-393`/`P-394` ship); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (test-only `ProjectReference`s, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.MultiTenancy` and `SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults`, confirmed/added once each package's corrected default exists on disk — both packages are already heavily real-assembly-referenced by this project from earlier phases, e.g. `SK.00.ServiceDefaultsGovernance`/P-173, so a `ProjectReference` to at least `SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults` likely already exists; the implementer must verify rather than assume); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (architecture test contracts, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase)
- Deleted files: none

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. Both new checks are plain public-helper assertions over Mono.Cecil-resolved default property values / method-body call sites — not Roslyn analyzers, not `NetArchTest`/`ICustomRule` predicates. No new `SK` diagnostic ID is assigned, following the same "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention `SecureDefaultsAssertion`'s own first two methods and `SecurityArchitectureRules`'s four methods already established. SK0032 remains the next available sequential ID for a future genuine Roslyn analyzer — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. Both new methods are added to the EXISTING `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class (from `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390) — the fourth and fifth methods on that class, not a new class, applying the same "protect a hardened default/security decision from silent regression" family the class's own first two methods established.
2. `.AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultEquals(Type optionsType, string propertyName, IReadOnlyList<string> expectedValuesInOrder)` reuses the exact `Ldstr` literal-collection sub-technique already built for `.AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultExcludes` (collect every `Ldstr` operand appearing in the constructor-body array/collection-initializer feeding `propertyName`'s backing-field `Stfld`, in IL emission order) but performs an ORDER-SENSITIVE sequence-equality comparison against `expectedValuesInOrder` instead of a forbidden-intersection check. This is necessary — not a stylistic choice — because `TenantResolutionOptions.StrategyOrder`'s security property depends specifically on relative order under first-non-null-result-wins semantics: `[Header, Claim, Database]` and `[Claim, Header, Database]` contain identical elements but only the latter is secure. Fails if the collected sequence's length differs from `expectedValuesInOrder`'s length, or if any positional element differs (ordinal string comparison — `StrategyName` values are platform-defined constants, not user input, so no case-insensitive leniency here unlike the JWS-algorithm check in `.AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultExcludes`).
3. `.AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type calleeDeclaringType, string calleeMethodName)` introduces this domain's NEWEST Mono.Cecil technique — METHOD-BODY INVOCATION-PRESENCE ASSERTION, the inverse of every prior technique in this file. Every existing `ConditionList`/`ICustomRule` predicate and every existing `SecureDefaultsAssertion`/`SecurityArchitectureRules` method fails ON THE PRESENCE of an unwanted call site or value; this is the first check that fails ON THE ABSENCE of an expected one. Loads `declaringType`'s `TypeDefinition` via Mono.Cecil, locates the single method matching `methodName` (throws a distinct, clearly-worded setup exception — never a silent false pass or false fail — if zero or more than one method matches), and scans its instruction body for a `Call`/`Callvirt` instruction whose resolved `MethodReference.Name == calleeMethodName` and `DeclaringType.FullName == calleeDeclaringType.FullName`. Fails if no matching instruction is found.
4. Rule 3's technique is the correct one for locking a `[LoggerMessage]`-source-generated call site in place: the source generator emits a real static/instance partial-method body invoked via a plain `Call` IL instruction at the call site — structurally identical to any hand-written method call — so no special-casing for the source-generated origin is needed.
5. Both methods throw the same single aggregate assertion-exception shape as `AssertEnumPropertyDefaultEquals`/`AssertStringCollectionPropertyDefaultExcludes` — naming the property/method, the actual resolved state, and the expected state.
6. Caller-supplied everything, same discipline as every other method on this class: the consuming test project supplies `optionsType`/`declaringType` via `typeof(TenantResolutionOptions)`/the real `AddMtlsForwardedHeaderCertificate`-declaring type (test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.MultiTenancy`/`SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults`), and `expectedValuesInOrder`/`calleeDeclaringType`/`calleeMethodName` from the real, shipped corrected values once `P-393`/`P-394`/`P-395` land. `00.Governance` never references `SharedKernel.MultiTenancy`/`SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults` directly in production code (`00.Governance` references nothing) — only the test project does, test-only.
7. Real-assembly verification for BOTH checks is UNVERIFIABLE/non-gating on THIS phase's own completion, mirroring `SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`'s/`SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`'s own precedent exactly — this time against `13.ServiceDefaults` rather than `12.Security`. As of this phase's authoring, `13.ServiceDefaults/state-map.md` confirms P-393/P-394's Design tasks (D-20–D-27) are locked but Scaffold/Core/Tests/Docs remain Not Started — the corrected `StrategyOrder` default and the `ForwardedHeaderTrustBoundaryUnconfigured` warning call site do not exist in compiled code yet. Design, implementation, and all contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests proceed now; the GATING real-assembly re-verification is tracked as a Cross-Domain Dependency and completed in a follow-up pass — but per this domain's now-repeated experience (`SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`/`SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock` both found their stated dependency had already shipped by implementation time), the implementer MUST re-verify against `13.ServiceDefaults/state-map.md` directly rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing.
8. The real declaring type/method name for `AddMtlsForwardedHeaderCertificate` (and the exact class hosting it) is not yet fixed in `13.ServiceDefaults/CLAUDE.md`'s own shipped-source terms as of this phase's authoring — the implementer must confirm the real compiled type/method name against the shipped source before writing T-317/T-318, never assume a name from this document.

### File-Level Plan
