## Phase SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard — Governance: Mechanical CORS Wildcard-Origin-Plus-Credentials Guard <!-- phase-key: SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard -->

### Goal

`14.Presentation`'s WO-062 review dispatched a CORS policy convention builder, `AddSharedKernelCors` (P-404), and its own accompanying startup-time guard against combining a wildcard/always-allow origin policy with `AllowCredentials()` — a configuration ASP.NET Core's `CorsService` accepts at registration time but only rejects (silently, per-request) at request-handling time. This review cycle has repeatedly found that a security-relevant default or guard documented and unit-tested only inside its own producing domain is not durable — `12.Security`'s WO-057/WO-060 passes (`SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`/P-373, `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390) and `13.ServiceDefaults`'s WO-061 pass (`SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`/P-401) each found a hardened default or guard that a future edit could silently regress with every existing test in its OWN domain still green, because nothing outside that domain re-asserted the invariant against the real, compiled assembly. This phase applies the same lesson to `14.Presentation` for the first time, and adds a genuinely new Roslyn analyzer (the first sequential-block SK ID consumed since SK0031/WO-057) so the dangerous CORS shape is caught platform-wide at compile time, not only inside the one package that happens to own the convention builder.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` (new Roslyn analyzer, SK0032) and `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (sixth method on the existing `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class) — no `SharedKernel.Benchmarks`/`SharedKernel.Linter` change.
- New files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/CorsWildcardOriginWithCredentialsAnalyzer.cs`; a corresponding `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests` test file.
- Modified files: `SecureDefaultsAssertion.cs` (one new method, `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType`); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (contrived fixture fire/pass-path tests now; the real-assembly test added once `P-404` ships past Design); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi`, added once `P-404`'s Core phase exists on disk — the implementer must confirm whether this project already references `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi` from an earlier phase rather than assume it does not); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (diagnostic registry, architecture test contracts, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0032 | CorsWildcardOriginWithCredentials | Security | Warning | A `CorsPolicyBuilder`-typed receiver has both an `AllowCredentials()` call and, in the same local/parameter/field scope (single fluent chain or separate statements), either `AllowAnyOrigin()` or a `SetIsOriginAllowed(...)` call whose lambda argument is syntactically unconditional-true |

`AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType` (the new `SecureDefaultsAssertion` method) carries no SK ID — following the established "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention already applied to every other non-`ConditionList`/`ICustomRule` helper in this file (`PipelineOrderAssertion`, `LoggingEventIdIntegrityAssertion`, `WellKnownConstantOwnershipAssertion`, `SecureDefaultsAssertion`'s own first five methods). SK0033 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. `CorsWildcardOriginWithCredentialsAnalyzer` is a semantic-model-assisted analyzer (mirroring SK0011's minimal `GetTypeInfo`/`GetSymbolInfo` shape) — a syntax-only name match on `AllowAnyOrigin`/`AllowCredentials`/`SetIsOriginAllowed` would misfire against any unrelated type coincidentally exposing same-named methods, so the receiver must resolve to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Cors.Infrastructure.CorsPolicyBuilder` before any further check runs.
2. Detection covers TWO call shapes, not just one: (a) a single fluent invocation chain (`builder.AllowAnyOrigin().AllowCredentials()`), and (b) separate statements against the same local variable/parameter/field within one method or lambda body (`var p = new CorsPolicyBuilder(); p.AllowAnyOrigin(); p.AllowCredentials();`). Shape (b) is not optional — ASP.NET Core's own `options.AddPolicy(name, builder => {...})` configuration delegate is at least as commonly written as separate statements as a single chain, and `AddSharedKernelCors`'s own real implementation is the concrete shape this rule must eventually catch a regression in.
3. The `SetIsOriginAllowed` branch fires only when its lambda argument is SYNTACTICALLY unconditional-true — an `ExpressionBody` that is exactly the `true` `LiteralExpressionSyntax`, or a `BlockBody` consisting of exactly `return true;`. This is a documented, intentional scope limit (no data-flow/constant-propagation analysis, mirroring SK0028/`HealthCheckTagIntegrityRules`/`NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate`'s own documented limitations) — an indirect always-true path is not caught.
4. The same-scope tracking for shape (b) is bounded to a single method/lambda body — a builder reference passed into a separate helper method that calls `AllowCredentials()` elsewhere is not followed across the method boundary. Also a documented, intentional scope limit.
5. `SecureDefaultsAssertion.AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type expectedExceptionType)` is the sixth method on the EXISTING `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class (from `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390), not a new class — introduces a METHOD-BODY THROW-PRESENCE ASSERTION, a sibling to `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s invocation-presence-assertion technique (both fail on the ABSENCE of an expected element): scans the method body's IL for a `Newobj` constructing `expectedExceptionType` followed anywhere later by a `Throw` opcode. Reuses `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s proven closure-method-scanning extension (from T-318) — when the direct method body contains no match, it additionally scans every method on every nested type of `declaringType` whose name starts with `<{methodName}>b__`, since a startup validation guard is plausibly registered via a `PostConfigure`/`Validate`-style lambda, exactly like `AddMtlsForwardedHeaderCertificate`'s own real shape.
6. This is a presence check across the whole method body plus its closures, not a reachability/control-flow check tied to the specific dangerous-configuration branch — documented as an intentional limitation, mirroring every other presence-based technique in this file. It proves "the guard exists and constructs+throws the expected exception type," not "the guard is provably correct for every input" — the latter remains `14.Presentation`'s own unit-test responsibility.
7. Caller-supplied everything, same discipline as every other method on `SecureDefaultsAssertion`: the consuming test project supplies `declaringType` via the real `AddSharedKernelCors`-owning type (test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi`) and `expectedExceptionType` from `14.Presentation`'s real, shipped guard-exception type. `00.Governance` never references `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi` directly in production code — only the test project does, test-only.
8. Real-assembly verification for `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType` is UNVERIFIABLE/non-gating on THIS phase's own completion, mirroring `SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`'s/`SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`'s/`SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`'s own precedent exactly — this time against `14.Presentation` rather than `12.Security`/`13.ServiceDefaults`. As of this phase's authoring, `14.Presentation`'s P-404 is `◐` Dispatched (Design only, per the dispatcher's explicit note) — `AddSharedKernelCors` does not exist in compiled code yet. Design, implementation, and all contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests proceed now; the GATING real-assembly re-verification is tracked as a Cross-Domain Dependency — but per this domain's now-repeated experience (every prior phase in this family found its stated dependency had already shipped by implementation time), the implementer MUST re-verify against `14.Presentation/state-map.md` directly rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing.
9. SK0032 itself (the Roslyn analyzer) is NOT gated on `14.Presentation` at all — it is a platform-wide, source-level prohibition that applies the moment it ships, exactly like SK0013/SK0030/SK0031 before it. Only the SEPARATE `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType` real-assembly check (verifying `AddSharedKernelCors`'s own guard) is gated.
10. The real declaring type/method name for `AddSharedKernelCors`, and the real exception type its guard throws, are not yet fixed in `14.Presentation/CLAUDE.md`'s own shipped-source terms as of this phase's authoring — the implementer must confirm both against the shipped source before writing the real-assembly test, never assume a name from this document (mirrors `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`'s Rule 8 discipline exactly).

### File-Level Plan

|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers/Diagnostics/CorsWildcardOriginWithCredentialsAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0032 — detects wildcard/always-allow-origin combined with `AllowCredentials()` on the same `CorsPolicyBuilder` |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/...CorsWildcardOriginWithCredentialsAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire/pass-path tests for SK0032 (T-319–T-325) |

## Phase SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard — Governance: Mechanically Lock the Correlation-ID Caller-Input Validation Default <!-- phase-key: SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard -->

### Goal

`14.Presentation`'s WO-063 review dispatched `CorrelationIdOptions` (`MaxLength`/`AllowedCharacterPattern`) and a corresponding extension to `CorrelationIdMiddleware`'s resolution path (P-415) — rejecting/regenerating a caller-supplied correlation-id value that fails a length/character-allowlist check before it is committed to `Activity` baggage or the response header, closing an unvalidated-passthrough gap this review cycle's own research found. This domain has now repeatedly found (`12.Security` twice — `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`/P-373, `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390; `13.ServiceDefaults` — `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`/P-401; `14.Presentation`'s own CORS guard — `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`/P-410) that a security-relevant boundary check documented and unit-tested only inside its OWN producing domain is not durable — a future edit can silently regress it with every test in that domain still green, because nothing outside it re-asserts the invariant against the real, compiled assembly. This phase applies the identical lesson to `14.Presentation`'s correlation-id validation guard specifically, distinct from (and dispatched immediately after) that same domain's CORS guard already locked by `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`.

Unlike every phase in this "lock a not-yet-shipped hardened guard" family before it, this phase requires **zero new production code** in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` and **zero new SK diagnostic ID** — the shape P-415 describes (a validation check invoked before a value is committed, or a conditional value substitution) is structurally identical to two techniques this domain already built and proved necessary: `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod` (WO-061/P-401, invocation-presence assertion) and, as a documented fallback if the shipped guard instead throws, `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType` (WO-062/P-410, throw-presence assertion). This phase is deliberately designed to REUSE one of these rather than speculatively invent a third technique before the real shape is known — the same discipline the CORS phase itself was forced to apply retroactively when its assumed throw-based shape turned out to be a validator-based one instead.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` only (test project) — no `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (production), `SharedKernel.Benchmarks`, or `SharedKernel.Linter` change.
- New files: none.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (new contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests now; the real-assembly test added once `P-415` ships past Design into Core); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (confirm the existing test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi` — already added by `SK.00.PresentationArchRules`/`SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard` — still covers this new call site; no new reference expected); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Architecture Test Contracts section, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. This phase consumes no new SK ID — the check is a single specific real-assembly call-site assertion (mirroring `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`'s `AddMtlsForwardedHeaderCertificate` check and `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`'s `CorsPolicyOptionsValidator` check), not a general source-level anti-pattern a platform-wide Roslyn analyzer should catch. SK0033 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. Reuse the existing `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type calleeDeclaringType, string calleeMethodName)` (`SecureDefaultsAssertion`, WO-061/P-401) as the primary technique — no new Mono.Cecil technique, no new method on `SecureDefaultsAssertion`, no new SK ID. This is the first phase in the "lock a not-yet-shipped hardened guard" family to require zero new production code in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`, a deliberate outcome of picking the technique that already fits the shape `14.Presentation`'s own design (D-57/D-58, per its `state-map.md`) describes — a conditional check-then-substitute, not a distinct new mechanism.
2. The real declaring type is expected to be `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi`'s `CorrelationIdMiddleware`, method `ResolveCorrelationId` (per `14.Presentation/state-map.md`'s own D-58/C-65 wording) — but the exact validation-helper callee name (e.g. `CorrelationIdOptions.IsValid`, a private static regex-check helper, or similar) is NOT yet fixed, since P-415 is still `○` Design-only as of this phase's authoring. The implementer MUST confirm both the real declaring type/method name and the real callee against `14.Presentation`'s shipped source before writing the real-assembly test — never assume either from this document (mirrors `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`'s Rule 8 / `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`'s Rule 10 discipline exactly).
3. If the implementer instead finds the shipped guard rejects an invalid value by throwing rather than by conditionally invoking-then-substituting, `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType` (the sixth `SecureDefaultsAssertion` method, WO-062/P-410) is the correct fallback technique — mirroring the exact design/reality-mismatch resolution the CORS phase itself needed for `AddSharedKernelCors`. Do not add a third new method to `SecureDefaultsAssertion` speculatively; these two already cover both plausible shapes (conditional invocation-then-substitution, or an outright throw).
4. This is a presence-only check, not a full control-flow/ordering verification — it cannot structurally distinguish "the validation call happens before the baggage/header commit" from "the validation call happens somewhere in the method, in any order." This is a DOCUMENTED, INTENTIONAL limitation, consistent with every other presence-based technique already in this file (`AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s and `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType`'s own identical documented scope). The acceptance bar this check proves is "the validation call site still exists in the method," not "the validation is provably applied before every commit path" — the latter remains `14.Presentation`'s own unit-test responsibility (its own T-55/T-56/T-57, per its `state-map.md`, already cover the runtime behavior end-to-end).
5. Real-assembly verification is UNVERIFIABLE/non-gating on this phase's own completion — `14.Presentation`'s P-415 is confirmed `○` Design-only (D-57/S-25/C-64/C-65 all `○` Pending, per `14.Presentation/state-map.md` read directly) as of this phase's authoring, mirroring `SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard`'s/`SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`'s/`SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`'s/`SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`'s own precedent exactly. Design and contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests proceed now; the GATING real-assembly test is tracked as a Cross-Domain Dependency — but per this domain's now-repeatedly-confirmed experience (every prior phase in this family found its stated dependency had already shipped by implementation time), the implementer MUST re-verify against `14.Presentation/state-map.md` directly rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing.
6. `calleeDeclaringType`, if the validation logic lives on a type not directly `typeof`-accessible (e.g. an internal helper), is resolved via `declaringType.Assembly.GetType("Full.Namespace.Type")` rather than `typeof(...)`, mirroring `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s own established precedent for an inaccessible internal type (`ServiceDefaultsLog`, `CorrelationIdOptionsValidator`-shaped internal validators).
7. `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s existing closure-method-scanning extension (proven necessary by T-318, reused as-is by T-328) already covers the case where the validation call is hosted inside a lambda closure rather than the method's own direct IL body — no further extension is anticipated to be necessary here, but the implementer must still confirm this against the real shipped shape rather than assume it.

### File-Level Plan

| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify | New contrived fixture fire/pass-path tests reusing `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod` (or `AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType` fallback); real-assembly test added once `P-415` ships past Design into Core |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Confirm | Verify the existing test-only `ProjectReference` (`PrivateAssets="all"`) to `SharedKernel.Presentation.WebApi` already covers this new call site — no new reference expected |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A contrived fixture test proves `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod` PASSES when a fixture method body calls the expected validation-helper method before returning/assigning a value

Requires `14.Presentation` P-415 (`CorrelationIdMiddleware`'s format-validation logic implemented past Design, i.e. Core phase complete) before the one real-assembly re-verification test can be written — tracked below under Cross-Domain Dependencies. **IMPLEMENTATION-ORDER NOTE:** this phase's contrived-fixture tests do not require `14.Presentation` source to exist and may proceed immediately. Do NOT attempt the real-assembly test until `14.Presentation/state-map.md` confirms P-415's Core phase (not merely Design) is complete.

## Phase SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock — Governance: Mechanically Lock the SSRF-Safe Delivery Default <!-- phase-key: SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock -->

### Goal

`15.Integration`'s WO-064 review dispatched `IWebhookUrlValidator`/`PrivateNetworkWebhookUrlValidator` (P-422) — a default, fail-closed guard rejecting an outbound webhook delivery target whose DNS-resolved IP address falls inside a private/loopback/link-local/cloud-metadata range, invoked immediately before every `SendAsync` call inside `WebhookDispatcher.DispatchToSubscriptionAsync`, overridable only via an explicit `WithUrlValidator<T>()` opt-out or `WebhookDeliveryOptions.AllowPrivateNetworkTargets`. This review cycle has now found the identical "a security-relevant default, once designed, needs a mechanical lock or it silently regresses under a later refactor with every existing test still green" pattern SIX times (`12.Security` twice — `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`/P-373, `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390; `13.ServiceDefaults` once — `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`/P-401; `14.Presentation` twice — `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`/P-410, `SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard`/P-420). An SSRF guard protecting outbound HTTP delivery to a consumer-supplied URL is exactly this class of fact — the platform's first webhook/outbound-delivery-domain application of the lesson, and (per the phase input's own framing) worth pinning permanently precisely because a future refactor of `WebhookDispatcher`/`AddSharedKernelWebhooks` could silently drop the default registration or weaken the range check with every `15.Integration`-owned unit test still passing (those tests exercise the guard via a spy/fake `IWebhookUrlValidator`, per `15.Integration/CLAUDE.md`'s own H-08 design, so they cannot themselves prove the REAL `PrivateNetworkWebhookUrlValidator` stays wired in or stays correct).

Unlike every phase in this family so far, this one has TWO independent things to lock, not one: (1) that `AddSharedKernelWebhooks()` still registers a default `IWebhookUrlValidator` implementation at all (a structural DI-registration-presence fact, the same shape as `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`'s `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`/`SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`'s `NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate`), and (2) that the registered default's range-membership logic is genuinely fail-closed for the documented ranges (a COMPUTED BEHAVIOR, not a structural fact any prior technique in this file was designed to prove). These are deliberately handled by two different techniques rather than forced into one — see Implementation Rules.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (production — one new method on the existing `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class) and `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` (test project). No `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.Benchmarks`, or `SharedKernel.Linter` change — no new Roslyn analyzer, no new SK diagnostic ID.
- New files: possibly a new test file for the executed Technique B behavioral test (e.g. `WebhookSsrfGuardTests.cs`), implementer's choice — may instead live inside the existing `SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs`.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/.../SecureDefaultsAssertion.cs` (new method); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (new contrived fixture tests now; real-assembly tests once `15.Integration`'s P-422 ships past Design into Core); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (new test-only `ProjectReference`, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to `SharedKernel.Integration.Webhooks`, once it exists as a real buildable assembly); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Architecture Test Contracts section, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. This phase consumes no new SK ID — both techniques are real-assembly regression-lock checks (a DI-registration-presence fact and an executed-behavior fact), not source-level anti-patterns a platform-wide Roslyn analyzer should catch, following the same "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention as every phase in this family. SK0033 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. Extend the EXISTING `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class (not a new class) with one new method — Technique A — `AssertMethodBodyRegistersSingleton(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type serviceType, Type implementationType)`. This generalizes/INVERTS `SecurityArchitectureRules.NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate`'s (WO-057/P-373) generic-instance-method-argument inspection technique (`GenericInstanceMethod.GenericArguments`) from "assert ABSENCE of a singleton registration for a forbidden type" to "assert PRESENCE of a singleton registration for exactly the given service→implementation pair." Loads `declaringType`'s `TypeDefinition`, locates the single method matching `methodName` (throws a distinct setup exception, never a silent false pass/fail, if zero or more than one method matches — mirroring `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s own established discipline), and scans its instruction body — plus, reusing `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s proven closure-scanning extension (T-318/T-328), every method on every nested type whose name starts with `<{methodName}>b__` — for a `Call`/`Callvirt` instruction whose resolved `MethodReference.Name == "AddSingleton"` and whose `GenericInstanceMethod.GenericArguments` equal `[serviceType, implementationType]` in that order. Fails if no matching instruction is found.
2. The real declaring type is expected to be the DI extension class hosting `AddSharedKernelWebhooks` inside `SharedKernel.Integration.Webhooks` (per `15.Integration/CLAUDE.md`'s own `Extensions/` folder listing), and `serviceType`/`implementationType` are expected to be `IWebhookUrlValidator`/`PrivateNetworkWebhookUrlValidator` — but the exact declaring class NAME is not yet fixed, since P-422 (H-06 through H-09) is confirmed `○` Not started as of this phase's authoring. The implementer MUST confirm the real declaring type/method name against `15.Integration`'s shipped source before writing the real-assembly test, never assume either from this document — mirrors the now-repeated "confirm, never assume" discipline (Rule 2 of `SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard`, Rule 8 of `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`, Rule 10 of `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`).
3. `AddSharedKernelWebhooks`'s registration is expected to use the plain `AddSingleton<TService,TImplementation>()` overload, not `TryAddSingleton` — `15.Integration/CLAUDE.md`'s own design prose states `WithUrlValidator<T>()` "overrides the default … registration — the last call wins," which is plain-`AddSingleton`'s last-registration-wins DI resolution behavior, not `TryAdd`'s first-registration-wins behavior. If the shipped code instead uses `TryAddSingleton` (`Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions`), the implementer must widen the registration-method-name match accordingly (a second accepted literal, not a rewrite) — confirm against real source, do not assume.
4. Fail-closed range behavior — the second half of this phase's acceptance criterion — is DELIBERATELY NOT implemented as a new static-IL `SecureDefaultsAssertion` method. Every one of that class's existing methods proves a STRUCTURAL fact (a constant's value, a call site's presence, a throw's presence); "rejects the documented private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP ranges" is a COMPUTED BEHAVIOR of arbitrary range-membership logic whose concrete representation (CIDR string literals fed to `IPNetwork.Parse`, hardcoded `IPAddress`/byte-array comparisons, or something else) is not yet fixed by `15.Integration`'s Design-only P-422 — no sound, representation-agnostic static technique exists for this half of the check. This phase's GATING real-assembly verification for range behavior is instead Technique B, a genuinely EXECUTED test — the first of its kind in this file, a deliberate, explicitly-flagged departure from `SecureDefaultsAssertion`'s "IL-only, never execute the assembly under test" discipline followed by all of its existing methods — living directly in a test file (`SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` or a new sibling file, implementer's choice) rather than as a reusable helper method on the class itself, since it is a one-off assertion tied to one real type rather than a general-purpose technique a future lock could reuse.
5. Technique B resolves the real, compiled `PrivateNetworkWebhookUrlValidator` (via its public constructor if parameterless/simple, or DI-container resolution against a minimal `ServiceCollection` built from `AddSharedKernelWebhooks()` if its constructor requires injected dependencies) and invokes its public `IWebhookUrlValidator` contract method against a fixed table of representative targets — at minimum one loopback address (`127.0.0.1`), one RFC 1918 private address (`10.0.0.1`), one link-local/cloud-metadata address (`169.254.169.254` — the AWS/Azure/GCP instance-metadata endpoint, SSRF's single most common real-world target), and one public-internet control address (`8.8.8.8`) — asserting rejection for the first three and acceptance for the fourth. Uses IP-literal hosts exclusively (never a DNS hostname) so the test never performs an actual network round-trip, remaining fully deterministic and offline — mirroring `15.Integration`'s own H-08 test-design constraint ("never a real DNS lookup or network call") applied here to a governance test instead of a domain test.
6. If the real `PrivateNetworkWebhookUrlValidator`'s public entry point still calls `Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync` even for an already-valid IP-literal host (some implementations resolve unconditionally before checking `IPAddress.TryParse`), the implementer should exercise that path exactly as a real caller would rather than reaching for an internal-only fast path — `Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync` against an IP-literal host resolves purely locally per BCL contract, with no actual network I/O, so this does not compromise Rule 5's "offline, deterministic" requirement.
7. Both techniques are UNVERIFIABLE/GATING against the real, compiled `SharedKernel.Integration.Webhooks` assembly as of this phase's authoring — `15.Integration`'s P-422 (H-06 through H-09) is confirmed `○` Not started (per `15.Integration/state-map.md`, read directly, not assumed). Design and all contrived fire/pass/boundary-path fixture tests for Technique A proceed now (Technique A only — Technique B has no static contrived-fixture substitute, per Rule 4); both real-assembly GATING tests are tracked as a new Cross-Domain Dependencies block, not force-failed or silently deferred — per this domain's now-six-times-repeated experience, the implementer MUST re-verify against `15.Integration/state-map.md` directly at implementation time rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing.
8. No new SK diagnostic ID — this is a real-assembly regression-lock rule on an already-designed guard's default configuration and registration, not a source-level anti-pattern a Roslyn analyzer should catch, following the established "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention of every phase in this family. ## Phase SK.00.CacheEncryptionAndRedisValidationLock — Governance: Mechanically Lock Cache-Encryption Ordering and Redis Secure-Transport Defaults <!-- phase-key: SK.00.CacheEncryptionAndRedisValidationLock -->

### Goal

`02.Caching`'s WO-065 review dispatched two hardening phases: `AddCacheEncryption()` (its own Phase 42/P-433), composing an opt-in compression stage and an opt-in encryption stage into one cache-value pipeline, with a documented invariant that compression must always be applied before encryption — reversing this order silently defeats compression's size benefit, since compressing already-encrypted (high-entropy) bytes yields little to no size reduction; and `AddRedisConnection` (its own Phase 45/P-436), adding startup-time options validation to the Redis connection surface. This review cycle has now found the identical "a security- or correctness-relevant default, once designed, needs a mechanical lock or it silently regresses under a later refactor with every existing test still green" pattern EIGHT times (`12.Security` twice — `SK.00.SecurityContextGuard`/P-373, `SK.00.SecureDefaultsLock`/P-390; `13.ServiceDefaults` once — `SK.00.TenantAndMtlsBoundaryLock`/P-401; `14.Presentation` twice — `SK.00.CorsWildcardCredentialsGuard`/P-410, `SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard`/P-420; `15.Integration` once — `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`/P-432). This phase applies the identical lesson to `02.Caching` for the first time, and BROADENS the family's scope beyond a pure security vulnerability to a correctness/efficiency regression — the ordering contract this phase locks mirrors the one `07.Messaging`'s own opt-in payload transform already documents in the root `CLAUDE.md` ("compress-then-encrypt order on publish and the reverse on consume," P-346), so `02.Caching`'s version of the same pattern deserves the same mechanical protection.

Unlike every phase in this family so far except `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`, this one has TWO independent things to lock, not one: (1) that `AddCacheEncryption()`'s composed pipeline genuinely applies compression before encryption (a COMPUTED BEHAVIOR of two composed pipeline stages, the same class of fact `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`'s Technique B proved no sound static IL technique can honestly capture), and (2) that `AddRedisConnection`'s options validation genuinely executes eagerly at host startup rather than merely decorating `RedisConnectionOptions` with inert `DataAnnotations` attributes (a STRUCTURAL call-site-presence fact, the same shape `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod` already proves elsewhere in this file). These are deliberately handled by two different techniques rather than forced into one — see Implementation Rules.

Both `02.Caching` dependencies (P-433/P-436) were still in the PLANNING stage — not yet dispatched for implementation — at this phase's authoring. This phase is designed against `02.Caching/state-map.md`'s own Phase 42/Phase 45 descriptions, per the dispatching agent's explicit note, exactly as every prior phase in this family has been designed against a not-yet-shipped (or, twice now, not-yet-implemented) dependency.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` only (test project) — no `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (production), `SharedKernel.Benchmarks`, or `SharedKernel.Linter` change, and no new method added to the existing `SecureDefaultsAssertion` class.
- New files: possibly a new test file for Technique A's executed behavioral test (e.g. `CacheEncryptionOrderingTests.cs`), implementer's choice — may instead live inside the existing `SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs`, mirroring `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`'s own file-placement discretion.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (new contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests for Technique B now; both real-assembly tests added once `02.Caching`'s P-433/P-436 ship past Design into Core); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (new test-only `ProjectReference`s, `PrivateAssets="all"`, to whichever `SharedKernel.Caching.*` package(s) host `AddCacheEncryption()`/`AddRedisConnection`, once they exist as real buildable assemblies); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Architecture Test Contracts section, Implementation Rules, changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. This phase consumes no new SK ID — both techniques are real-assembly regression-lock checks (a computed composition-ordering behavior and a call-site-presence fact), not source-level anti-patterns a platform-wide Roslyn analyzer should catch, following the established "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention of every phase in this family. SK0033 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID — not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. Technique A (compress-then-encrypt composition ordering) is DELIBERATELY NOT implemented as a new `SecureDefaultsAssertion` method, for the same reason `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`'s Technique B was not — "compression demonstrably ran before encryption" is a COMPUTED BEHAVIOR of two composed pipeline stages whose concrete representation (a decorator pair over `ICacheSerializer`, a single combined transform delegate, or something else) is not yet fixed by `02.Caching`'s still-planning-stage Phase 42. No sound, representation-agnostic static IL technique exists for this half of the check. Instead this is the SECOND genuinely EXECUTED real-assembly test in this file (after `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`'s Technique B) — a deliberate, explicitly-flagged departure from `SecureDefaultsAssertion`'s "IL-only, never execute the assembly under test" discipline — living directly in a test file rather than as a reusable helper method, since it is a one-off assertion tied to one real pipeline rather than a general-purpose technique a future lock could reuse.
2. Technique A builds the real, compiled `AddCacheEncryption()`-composed pipeline via a minimal `IServiceCollection`, with both compression and encryption enabled and a fixed test key/options, then serializes a HIGHLY COMPRESSIBLE payload (e.g. a string of at least 1KB of a repeated character) through it and captures the final byte length that would be persisted to the underlying store. It separately encrypts the SAME payload directly via `01.Core`'s existing `ISymmetricEncryptionService` (no compression) as a baseline, measuring its byte length, and asserts the pipeline's output length is meaningfully smaller than that baseline (below a fixed ratio threshold, e.g. under 50%) — proving compression measurably ran before/around encryption. If the real composition order were reversed (encrypt-then-attempt-compress), compressing high-entropy ciphertext yields near-zero size reduction — a well-known property of general-purpose compression against high-entropy input — so this assertion correctly fails and catches the exact regression this phase exists to prevent. This is a BLACK-BOX, representation-agnostic technique: it assumes nothing about the pipeline's internal decorator/class names, only its public `AddCacheEncryption()` entry point and the resulting serialize/deserialize round trip.
3. Technique A also asserts a round-trip-correctness precondition — decrypting and decompressing the pipeline's stored bytes via its own read path recovers the original payload exactly — guarding against the size-reduction assertion accidentally passing against corrupted or no-op output rather than genuine compress-then-encrypt behavior.
4. DOCUMENTED LIMITATION (same class as `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`'s Technique B and every other technique in this file): a size-ratio threshold is a reliable, low-false-positive signal for any straightforward correct-vs-reversed implementation, not a byte-exact structural proof of instruction ordering. The acceptance bar this test proves is "the shipped pipeline's observable size behavior is consistent with compress-then-encrypt," not "the pipeline's IL provably calls Compress before Encrypt in every code path."
5. Technique B (redis options-validation eagerness) reuses the EXISTING `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type calleeDeclaringType, string calleeMethodName)` (`SecureDefaultsAssertion`, WO-061/P-401) unchanged — no new Mono.Cecil technique, no new method on `SecureDefaultsAssertion`, no new SK ID. This is the SECOND phase in this "lock a not-yet-shipped hardened guard" family to require zero new production code in `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests`, after `SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard`.
6. Technique B targets `declaringType` = `SharedKernel.Caching.Redis.Core.Extensions.RedisConnectionCoreExtensions` (confirmed on disk at implementation time — `02.Caching/SharedKernel.Caching.Redis.Core/Extensions/RedisConnectionCoreExtensions.cs`), `methodName` = `"AddRedisConnection"`, `calleeDeclaringType` = `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.OptionsBuilderExtensions` (CORRECTED at implementation time — this rule originally named `Microsoft.Extensions.Options.OptionsBuilderExtensions`; the real extension method `ValidateOnStart<TOptions>(this OptionsBuilder<TOptions>)` is declared in the `Microsoft.Extensions.Options` NuGet package but under the `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` namespace — confirmed by direct inspection before writing the real-assembly test, per this rule's own "confirm, never assume" instruction), `calleeMethodName` = `"ValidateOnStart"`. Proving a call to `ValidateOnStart()` is the correct way to distinguish GENUINE eager startup validation (the marker that causes `Microsoft.Extensions.Options`'s own host-startup validation machinery to run at `IHost.StartAsync()`) from an inert `[Required]`/`DataAnnotations` attribute on `RedisConnectionOptions` alone, or a registered `IValidateOptions<RedisConnectionOptions>` that validates only lazily on first options access without `.ValidateOnStart()` — exactly the acceptance criterion's own stated failure mode ("merely decorating the options type with inert attributes").
7. If the implementer finds the real shape instead wires a custom `IValidateOptions<RedisConnectionOptions>` WITHOUT a `.ValidateOnStart()` call anywhere in `AddRedisConnection`'s method body (or its closures, per Rule 9 below), this check correctly reports the gap by failing — that is itself the exact regression this phase exists to catch, not a false positive. Do not weaken the check to also accept a bare `IValidateOptions<T>` registration without `.ValidateOnStart()` — a validator registered but never triggered at startup is precisely "genuinely executes at startup" failing to hold.
8. `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s existing closure-method-scanning extension (proven necessary by T-318, reused as-is by T-328/T-331) already covers the case where the `.ValidateOnStart()` call is hosted inside a lambda closure (e.g. a fluent `services.AddOptions<RedisConnectionOptions>().Configure(...).ValidateOnStart()` chain compiled with intermediate closures) rather than the method's own direct IL body — no further extension is anticipated to be necessary, but the implementer must still confirm this against the real shipped shape rather than assume it.
9. Both techniques are UNVERIFIABLE/GATING against the real, compiled `SharedKernel.Caching.*` assemblies as of this phase's authoring — `02.Caching`'s P-433/P-436 are confirmed PLANNED (Phases 42/45 in `02.Caching/state-map.md`, per the dispatching agent's own explicit note) but not yet dispatched for implementation. Design and Technique B's contrived fire/pass-path fixture tests proceed now (Technique A has no static contrived-fixture substitute, per Rule 1, mirroring `SK.00.WebhookSsrfGuardLock`'s Rule 4 precedent exactly); both real-assembly GATING tests are tracked as a new Cross-Domain Dependencies block, not force-failed or silently deferred — per this domain's now-eight-times-repeated experience, the implementer MUST re-verify against `02.Caching/state-map.md` directly at implementation time rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing.
10. No new SK diagnostic ID — both techniques are real-assembly regression-lock checks on an already-designed pipeline/registration's behavior and configuration, not source-level anti-patterns a Roslyn analyzer should catch, following the established "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention of every phase in this family. SK0033 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID, not consumed here.

## Phase SK.00.MapperEnforcement — Governance: Endorse Mapperly, Forbid Reflection-Based Object Mapping <!-- phase-key: SK.00.MapperEnforcement -->

### Goal

`arch-lead` closed out the mapping-capability question (WO-079/P-486) with a REDIRECT, not a straight accept: it declined to ship a `SharedKernel.Mapping` package — wrapping Mapperly, a compile-time source generator, behind a kernel-owned runtime interface would defeat the entire reason to choose it over AutoMapper — and asked this domain to mechanize only the genuinely shared-kernel-appropriate half of the decision: a platform-wide prohibition on reflection-based mapping libraries. Root `CLAUDE.md`'s "What Goes Where" table already carries the corresponding guidance row (added by the dispatching pass), naming Mapperly and hand-written mapping as the sanctioned choices — this phase is purely the mechanical enforcement half.

This is the first phase in this file whose motivating capability is a DECLINED package, not a pending or shipped one — there is no `SharedKernel.Mapping` state-map to track a dependency against, and none will ever exist.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests`.
- New files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers/ReflectionBasedObjectMapperUsageAnalyzer.cs`; `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/ReflectionBasedObjectMapperUsageAnalyzerTests.cs`.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests.csproj` (new test-only `PackageReference`s — `AutoMapper`, and `Riok.Mapperly` for a realistic pass-path fixture); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Diagnostic Rule Registry SK0033 entry, Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0033 | ReflectionBasedObjectMapperUsage | Usage | Warning | AutoMapper `Profile` subclass / `IMapperConfigurationExpression` usage / `.AddAutoMapper(...)` call, each resolved by exact `ContainingAssembly.Name == "AutoMapper"` semantic-model match — never a syntax-only simple-name check, since "Profile" collides with legitimate unrelated types elsewhere in consuming services |

### Implementation Rules

1. All three trigger shapes require semantic-model resolution to the real `AutoMapper` assembly (mirrors SK0025's `ContainingAssembly.Name` exact-match technique) — a syntax-only `BaseList` name check on `"Profile"` would misfire against unrelated user-defined `Profile` types.
2. Mapster is DELIBERATELY NOT enforced. Its runtime-adapter and source-generated-adapter call syntax (`.Adapt<T>()`/`.BuildAdapter()`) is identical regardless of whether `Mapster.SourceGenerator` is installed — there is no reliable syntactic or semantic-model discriminator between the two modes. Ship AutoMapper-only rather than a rule with an uncontrolled false-positive rate against a legitimate Mapster source-generated consumer. Document this scope limit prominently in the diagnostic's `Limitation` field (already applied in `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`).
3. Fires globally — no suppression namespace. AutoMapper has no legitimate call site anywhere on this platform (its `Profile`/`IMapperConfigurationExpression`/`AddAutoMapper` API has no owning `SharedKernel.*` package the way `SharedKernel.Communication.Rest` legitimately owns `HttpClient` construction for SK0013).
4. No new `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` artifact — a per-compilation-unit source-level pattern the Roslyn analyzer resolves completely on its own, mirroring SK0030's "no architecture-test counterpart by design" precedent.
5. Fully ungated — needs no compiled reference to any not-yet-shipped SharedKernel package. `SharedKernel.Analyzers` itself takes zero new NuGet dependency (Roslyn analyzers detect third-party assembly identity via `Compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName`, no compile-time reference needed); only `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests` needs a test-only `PackageReference` to the real `AutoMapper` package (and, for a realistic pass-path fixture proving Mapperly composition explicitly does not trigger, `Riok.Mapperly`) for fixture compilation.
6. Confirm no `Directory.Packages.props` entry for `AutoMapper`/`Mapster`/`Riok.Mapperly` exists anywhere in this repo before implementation — verified clean at this phase's authoring (2026-08-26); if a future session finds one, treat it as a signal to re-open this design, not silently proceed.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers/ReflectionBasedObjectMapperUsageAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0033 — three-shape AutoMapper detection |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/ReflectionBasedObjectMapperUsageAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire-path (×3 shapes) and pass-path (×2: Mapperly, hand-written) tests |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests.csproj` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Modify | New test-only `PackageReference`s: `AutoMapper`, `Riok.Mapperly` |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | SK0033 diagnostic entry, Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Analyzer flags an AutoMapper `Profile` subclass, `IMapperConfigurationExpression` usage, or `.AddAutoMapper(...)` call anywhere in a production project
- [ ] Analyzer does not flag Mapster's adapter API in either mode — documented as an intentional scope limit, not an oversight
- [ ] A real-assembly test proves the rule fires against a contrived offending sample referencing the real `AutoMapper` package
- [ ] Diagnostic message names Mapperly and hand-written mapping as the sanctioned alternatives
- [ ] No new `SharedKernel.Mapping`/`.Mapper` package exists anywhere in this repo as a result of this phase

### Dependencies

- Requires: none — fully ungated, per Implementation Rule 5.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally; closes WO-079/P-486 end to end together with `arch-lead`'s own root `CLAUDE.md` "What Goes Where" row (already applied by the dispatching pass, not this phase's own scope).

- `Riok.Mapperly`: optional test-only `PackageReference` for a realistic pass-path fixture — never a production dependency of any `SharedKernel.*` package.

## Phase SK.00.MoneyCurrencyAdvisory — Governance: Advisory Rule Against Hand-Rolled Amount+Currency Pairs <!-- phase-key: SK.00.MoneyCurrencyAdvisory -->

### Goal

`03.Domain`'s new `Money` value object (P-439/WO-066, design-locked) gives the platform a canonical currency-aware monetary type for the first time. Following the platform's established habit of adding a guardrail against regressing to the pattern a new canonical type replaces (the hand-rolled-hashing ban after `SharedKernel.Cryptography` shipped, the raw-`HttpClient` ban after typed clients shipped), this phase nudges toward `Money` whenever a type declares a raw `decimal`-shaped monetary property alongside a raw `string`-shaped currency-code property.

Unlike every prior enforcement rule in this registry, this one is EXPLICITLY advisory and permanently so — it introduces the registry's first ADVISORY category, with no escalation path to Error, ever. The phase input itself frames the rule as inherently heuristic (a decimal+string co-occurrence cannot be detected with zero false positives) and asks for an advisory-only shape with a documented suppression path — this is a considered judgment call to ship a narrowly-scoped, empirically-validated heuristic, not a default assumption that every proposed rule ships. The detection technique (same-type co-occurrence of a closed suffix list on each side, syntax-only) is judged narrow enough to be worth shipping, distinct from the four capabilities `arch-lead` already declined this session on non-mechanical-detectability grounds — see Implementation Rules for the empirical-validation contingency that keeps this judgment honest rather than merely asserted.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests`.
- New files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers/AmountCurrencyPairAdvisoryAnalyzer.cs`; `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/AmountCurrencyPairAdvisoryAnalyzerTests.cs`.
- Modified files: `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Diagnostic Rule Registry SK0034 entry — first Advisory category, Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0034 | AmountCurrencyPairCoupling | Advisory (NEW — no escalation path to Error, ever) | Warning | Same type declares a `decimal`/`decimal?` member ending in `Amount`/`Price`/`Total`/`Balance` AND a `string`/`string?` member ending in `Currency`/`CurrencyCode`; self-exempt when the type is literally named `Money` |

### Implementation Rules

1. Syntax-only detection (`PredefinedTypeSyntax`/`NullableTypeSyntax` wrapping the `decimal`/`string` keyword) — no `SemanticModel` needed, since these are BCL keyword types resolvable from syntax alone.
2. Scan only DIRECT (non-inherited) `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`/`FieldDeclarationSyntax` members of a `class`/`record`/`struct` declaration — never `interface` (contract-only signatures generate excessive, low-value noise) and never inherited members (a base-type property shouldn't cause every derived type to re-flag).
3. Suffix lists are CLOSED and exactly as specified in the phase input: decimal side — `Amount`, `Price`, `Total`, `Balance`; string side — `Currency`, `CurrencyCode`. Case-sensitive PascalCase suffix match.
4. Self-exemption: a type whose own identifier is exactly `Money` never fires, regardless of its members — defensive hygiene even though `03.Domain`'s real `Money` type's `Currency` property is typed `Currency` (a value object), not `string`, so it would not structurally trigger anyway.
5. This rule's ADVISORY category is new to this registry and MUST NOT be treated as a stepping stone to Error severity in any future phase without a fresh design review — its detection technique cannot meet the near-zero false-positive bar every Error-severity rule on this platform requires. Document this explicitly wherever the rule is referenced.
6. MANDATORY empirical validation (T-350, Acceptance Criteria): before closing the Tests phase, run the analyzer against every already-shipped `SharedKernel.*` production assembly's source and record the raw hit list in the Docs phase. If that scan surfaces a genuine false positive (a decimal+string pair that is clearly not an amount/currency concept), narrow the suffix list — e.g. drop `Total`/`Balance`, keeping only `Amount`/`Price` + `Currency`/`CurrencyCode` — and re-run before shipping, rather than accepting the broader list on the strength of design-time reasoning alone. This scan can and should run NOW, before `03.Domain`'s `Money` ships — it validates against CURRENT sources, which by definition predate `Money` and therefore cannot contain a "correct" match to exclude.
7. Suppression is the standard built-in Roslyn mechanism (`#pragma warning disable SK0034` / a `.editorconfig` severity override) — no bespoke suppression attribute is needed; document this explicitly as satisfying the phase input's "documented suppression mechanism" acceptance criterion.
8. No new `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` artifact — a per-compilation-unit source-level heuristic, mirroring SK0030's/SK0033's "no architecture-test counterpart by design" precedent.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers/AmountCurrencyPairAdvisoryAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0034 — syntax-only same-type suffix co-occurrence heuristic |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/AmountCurrencyPairAdvisoryAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire-path, pass-path, self-exemption, and real-source false-positive validation tests |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | SK0034 diagnostic entry (Advisory category), Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Analyzer ships as warning-severity, not error-severity, with a documented suppression mechanism
- [ ] False-positive rate validated against this repo's own codebase and at least one representative sample project before shipping (T-350)
- [ ] Rule is documented as advisory in `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`, explicitly distinguished from the platform's error-level "prohibited" rules

### Dependencies

- Requires: none for the analyzer's own detection logic, which references no compiled `SharedKernel.Domain` type. Depends on `03.Domain` P-439 (`Money`) only so the diagnostic's remediation message can name a real, shipped type by the time this ships — verify `03.Domain/state-map.md` directly at implementation time rather than assuming either way, per this domain's now well-established re-verify discipline.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally; a terminal advisory nudge, mirroring this file's other "boundary/regression rule" phases' own closure shape.

### Tooling Version Notes

- No new NuGet dependency — syntax-only detection against BCL keyword types.
- Target framework: `netstandard2.0` (`SharedKernel.Analyzers`) / `net10.0` (`SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests`).

## Phase SK.00.DataPrivacyLoggingGuard — Governance: Flag an Unmasked Classified Member at a Logging Call Site <!-- phase-key: SK.00.DataPrivacyLoggingGuard -->

### Goal

`01.Core`'s new `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy` package (P-474/WO-076, design-locked) ships `[DataClassification]`/`[SensitiveDataCategory]` marker attributes and pure `PiiMasking.*` helpers — metadata whose SOLE sanctioned compile-time consumer is this domain's own governance tooling, per that package's own design ("never read via reflection in production code — sole sanctioned consumer is 00.Governance's compile-time analyzer and human documentation"). This phase is that consumer: a semantic-model analyzer flagging a classified member reaching a `[LoggerMessage]` call-site argument (or a whole classified-bearing type passed for `{@Param}`-style destructuring) without first passing through a `PiiMasking.*` call.

This is deliberately the ONE piece of the data-privacy story this domain mechanically enforces. The rest of the convention (classification taxonomy correctness, masking-helper correctness, data-subject-request handling) stays a documented convention rather than a mechanically-enforced rule, per this domain's established "decline unenforceable rules rather than ship weak ones" precedent — the same judgment `arch-lead` applied when it declined four other capabilities this session on non-mechanical-detectability grounds. This one earns real enforcement because it is a static attribute cross-referenced against a static call-site shape — genuinely, mechanically Roslyn-detectable with a controlled false-positive surface, unlike (for example) a fully general PII-leakage data-flow analysis would be.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests`.
- New files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers/UnmaskedClassifiedDataLoggingAnalyzer.cs`; `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/UnmaskedClassifiedDataLoggingAnalyzerTests.cs`.
- Modified files: `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Diagnostic Rule Registry SK0035 entry, Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase, Cross-Domain Dependencies).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0035 | UnmaskedClassifiedDataAtLoggingCallSite | Security | Warning | A `[LoggerMessage]`-attributed method call's argument resolves to a member carrying `DataClassification(Restricted)`/`SensitiveDataCategory(...)`, not wrapped in a `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy.PiiMasking.*` call first — resolved by fully-qualified metadata name, not a compiled reference |

### Implementation Rules

1. Trigger: an `InvocationExpressionSyntax` whose resolved method symbol carries `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerMessageAttribute` (the platform's sole sanctioned logging authoring shape, SK0020/SK0021). For each non-special argument (excluding `this ILogger`/`LogLevel`/`Exception`), resolve the argument expression via `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo`; if it resolves to a property/field symbol carrying `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy.DataClassificationAttribute` (Classification == Restricted) or `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy.SensitiveDataCategoryAttribute` (any category), AND the argument is not itself an invocation of a method whose `ContainingType` is exactly `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy.PiiMasking`, report the diagnostic.
2. Additionally cover the whole-object `{@ParamName}` destructuring shape: an argument whose STATIC TYPE declares any member carrying either attribute, passed directly with no masking call — this generalizes Rule 1 to catch passing an entire classified-bearing DTO/entity, not only a single classified property reference.
3. Resolve `DataClassificationAttribute`/`SensitiveDataCategoryAttribute`/`PiiMasking` by FULLY-QUALIFIED METADATA NAME (`Compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("SharedKernel.DataPrivacy.DataClassificationAttribute")`, etc.), NOT via a compiled `ProjectReference` — the same technique WO-040/P-248's marker-interface rules (SK0017–SK0019) established. This means Design/Core/contrived-fixture Tests proceed NOW: a test fixture declares its OWN fixture-local `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy` namespace with matching type names inside the same test compilation, requiring no `ProjectReference` to the not-yet-shipped real package.
4. A REAL-ASSEMBLY re-verification test — re-pointing the metadata-name resolution at the actual compiled `SharedKernel.DataPrivacy` package and real `SharedKernel.*` production log call sites — is GATING but genuinely deferred, tracked as a new Cross-Domain Dependencies entry below, not force-failed or silently skipped. Per this domain's now nine-times-repeated experience, the implementer MUST re-verify against `01.Core/state-map.md` directly at implementation time rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing.
5. Scope limit (documented, intentional, mirrors SK0028/`HealthCheckTagIntegrityRules`'s "pattern/presence check, not full data-flow analysis" convention): only a DIRECT member reference or a direct `PiiMasking.*` wrapper call is recognized. An intermediate local variable or a helper method that internally reads a classified member and returns it unmasked is not traced across that boundary.
6. No new `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` artifact for the analyzer itself — a per-compilation-unit source-level check the Roslyn analyzer resolves completely on its own once the real assembly exists for re-verification.

### File-Level Plan

| File | Package | Action | Purpose |
|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers/UnmaskedClassifiedDataLoggingAnalyzer.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers | Create | SK0035 — classified-member-to-logging-argument provenance check |
| `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/UnmaskedClassifiedDataLoggingAnalyzerTests.cs` | SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests | Create | Fire-path, pass-path (masked), and pass-path (unclassified) contrived-fixture tests now; real-assembly test added once `01.Core`'s P-474 ships past Design into Core |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | SK0035 diagnostic entry, Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog (already applied) |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Analyzer flags a classified member reaching a `[LoggerMessage]` placeholder or `{@Object}` destructuring without passing through a `PiiMasking.*` call first
- [ ] A real-assembly test proves the rule fires against a contrived offending sample and passes when the value is masked first
- [ ] Diagnostic message names the sanctioned `PiiMasking.*` helper, mirroring SK0022's remediation-message style

### Dependencies

- Requires: none for design/Core/contrived-fixture Tests — proceeds immediately via the fully-qualified-metadata-name technique (Rule 3), fully unblocked. Requires `01.Core`'s P-474 shipped past Design into Core before the real-assembly re-verification test can be written — tracked below under Cross-Domain Dependencies. **IMPLEMENTATION-ORDER NOTE:** re-verify against `01.Core/state-map.md` directly rather than trusting this note's "not yet implemented" framing, per this domain's now-repeated experience that a stated dependency has often already shipped by implementation time.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally; a terminal, self-contained rule mirroring this file's other single-analyzer phases' own closure shape.

## Phase SK.00.GrpcErrorMappingGuard — Governance: Mechanically Lock the gRPC Server Error-Mapping Path <!-- phase-key: SK.00.GrpcErrorMappingGuard -->

### Goal

`14.Presentation`'s new `SharedKernel.Presentation.Grpc` package (P-468/WO-074, design-locked, Core not yet started) ships a canonical `Result<T>`-to-`RpcException` mapping path (`GrpcResultExtensions`/`GrpcStatusCodeMap`). This phase mechanically locks that path the same way SK0013 locked typed-client construction and P-199 locked `ProblemDetails` construction: forbidding a hand-constructed `new RpcException(new Status(...))`/`throw new RpcException(...)` at any gRPC service-method call site outside `SharedKernel.Presentation.Grpc` itself.

Re-verified directly against `14.Presentation/state-map.md` (rather than trusting the root state-map's "Depends on: P-468" framing at face value) per this domain's now nine-times-repeated "confirm, never assume a stated dependency actually blocks this phase's own work" discipline (`SK.00.SenderConstrainedCredentialGuard` through `SK.00.CacheEncryptionAndRedisValidationLock`): this analyzer needs no compiled reference to `SharedKernel.Presentation.Grpc` at all — only the standalone, already-available `Grpc.Core.Api` NuGet package. Unlike every phase in the `SecureDefaultsAssertion`-lock family, this one is genuinely, fully ungated from the start, not merely found-to-be-already-shipped at implementation time.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.Analyzers`, `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests`.
- New files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers/RawRpcExceptionConstructionAnalyzer.cs`; `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests/RawRpcExceptionConstructionAnalyzerTests.cs`.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests.csproj` (new test-only `PackageReference` to `Grpc.Core.Api`); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (Diagnostic Rule Registry SK0036 entry, Implementation Rules bullet, Changelog — already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

| ID | Rule Name | Category | Severity | Trigger Summary |
|----|-----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| SK0036 | RawRpcExceptionConstruction | Usage | Warning | `new RpcException(...)`/`new Status(...)` resolved by exact semantic-model type match to `Grpc.Core.RpcException`/`Grpc.Core.Status`, outside the `SharedKernel.Presentation.Grpc` namespace |

### Implementation Rules

1. Semantic-model exact-type resolution (`SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo`/`GetTypeInfo` on `ObjectCreationExpressionSyntax`) — NOT a syntax-only simple-name match. "Status" is a dangerously generic simple name (order/application status enums, etc.) elsewhere on this platform and in consuming services — the exact lesson SK0026 already recorded for "Kernel." SK0013's "HttpClient is unique enough to match syntactically" precedent does not transfer here.
2. Flag BOTH `new RpcException(...)` AND standalone `new Status(...)` construction (a bare `Status` may be built for later use, e.g. assigning to a trailer, without being immediately wrapped) — two constructed-type checks under one diagnostic ID, mirroring SK0022's/SK0024's multi-shape-one-ID precedent.

5. Diagnostic message names the sanctioned `Result<T>`-to-`RpcException` extension (`GrpcResultExtensions`, backed by `GrpcStatusCodeMap.Resolve`) by name, mirroring SK0022's remediation-message style.
6. UNGATED: `SharedKernel.Analyzers` itself needs no compiled reference to `SharedKernel.Presentation.Grpc` (a namespace-string exemption match needs no `ProjectReference`) and no dependency on `Grpc.AspNetCore`. Only `SharedKernel.Analyzers.Tests` needs a test-only `PackageReference` to the lightweight, standalone `Grpc.Core.Api` package (containing solely `RpcException`/`Status`/`StatusCode`, not the full server hosting stack) for fixture compilation — this package is already independently available and does NOT require `14.Presentation`'s P-468 to have shipped.

Pass-path fixture for "the sanctioned extension path does not trigger" (Acceptance Criteria) uses a PLAIN method-invocation shape (no direct `new RpcException`/`new Status` in the fixture) — this also needs no real `SharedKernel.Presentation.Grpc` reference, keeping the entire phase's test suite fully self-contained.
8. No new `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` artifact, mirroring SK0013's own shape (a construction-path prohibition needs no companion IL-level regression lock beyond the Roslyn analyzer itself).
