## Phase SK.00.SyncCryptoGateAndArgon2ConfinementLock — Governance: Mechanically Lock the Synchronous-Encryption Provider Gate and Confine the Argon2 Third-Party Dependency <!-- phase-key: SK.00.SyncCryptoGateAndArgon2ConfinementLock -->

### Goal

WO-081 gives `01.Core/SharedKernel.Cryptography` a synchronous-provider capability gate: `P-492` adds `ISynchronousEncryptionKeyProvider`/`EncryptionKeyProviderCapabilities`, gating `AesGcmEncryptionService`'s retained sync `Encrypt`/`Decrypt`/`EncryptToString`/`DecryptToString` behind a construction-time check that throws `NotSupportedException` (directing callers to the `*Async` overloads) instead of silently bridging via `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` against a KMS-backed provider — the exact shape that thread-pool-starves a caller. `P-493` mirrors the identical pattern for `IAsymmetricSignatureService`'s retained sync `Sign`/`Verify` via a second marker, `ISynchronousAsymmetricKeyProvider`/`AsymmetricKeyProviderCapabilities`. `P-495` adds a new sibling package, `SharedKernel.Cryptography.Argon2`, whose `Konscious.Security.Cryptography.Argon2` third-party dependency must never leak into the zero-third-party-dependency `SharedKernel.Cryptography` core — the same confinement invariant `SharedKernel.Cryptography.KeyVault.Azure` (P-447) already carries. This phase mechanically locks both, mirroring the `SecureDefaultsAssertion`-lock family's now nine-times-repeated "a security- or correctness-relevant default/guard documented only in prose eventually drifts" lesson — see `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md`'s `SecureDefaultsAssertion` "Tenth real-world application" entry and `CryptoIsolationRules.CryptographyCoreHasNoThirdPartyDependencies` entry for the full technical record; this section covers only the phase-management view.

Dispatched deliberately LAST in this WO-081 wave — `P-504` depends on `P-492`/`P-495`, both in `01.Core`, so the coordinator overrode `/dispatch-phase`'s domain-number-ascending sort to respect the real dependency. All eight upstream WO-081 domains are already design-locked this session.

**A critical honesty check this phase's own authoring took seriously, not merely rubber-stamped.** Every upstream domain in this wave is DESIGN-LOCKED ONLY as of this phase's authoring — no `C-*`/`T-*`/`DO-*`/`P-*` implementation task has shipped anywhere in WO-081. `16.Testing` verified directly on disk that `ISymmetricEncryptionService`/`IAsymmetricKeyProvider`/`IAsymmetricSignatureService` all still carry their pre-WO-081 signatures, and that no `ISynchronousEncryptionKeyProvider`/`EncryptionKeyProviderCapabilities` type exists anywhere in `01.Core/SharedKernel.Cryptography/` yet; `SharedKernel.Cryptography.Argon2` does not exist as a project at all. This domain has a documented precedent (SK0030's own GATING real-source audit) of verifying a rule against real shipped source before claiming it works — a rule written against types that do not yet exist cannot be verified non-vacuously. This phase therefore splits its two techniques by HONEST verifiability rather than treating them uniformly:

- **Technique A** (the synchronous-provider gate) is genuinely, fully UNVERIFIABLE today — one level further removed than every prior "designed against a not-yet-shipped dependency" occurrence in this family, where the producing domain had usually already shipped Core by implementation time (a 4-out-of-6-plus finding rate). Design and contrived fixture tests proceed now; the two real-assembly tests are tracked as GATING/deferred Cross-Domain Dependencies, never force-failed or silently skipped, per this domain's standing discipline.
- **Technique B** (Argon2/KeyVault.Azure dependency confinement) is, by contrast, FULLY VERIFIABLE TODAY — a genuine, evaluated finding, not a rubber-stamp of WO-081/P-504's own stated dependency on `P-495`. It targets the ALREADY-SHIPPED `SharedKernel.Cryptography` core assembly and is proven non-vacuous via a temporary reintroduced `Konscious.Security.Cryptography.Argon2` `PackageReference`, confirmed to fail, then reverted before commit — this is literally WO-081/P-504's own second acceptance criterion, achievable with zero dependency on `SharedKernel.Cryptography.Argon2` ever shipping.

**Two inputs surfaced by other WO-081 domain planners, both evaluated and folded into the design (not ignored):**

1. `07.Messaging` proved by reflection against the installed MassTransit assembly that its payload-transform serializer interfaces are hard-synchronous with no async overload anywhere — after `P-492` ships, that domain's sync `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` call site is structurally unavoidable and legitimate, not a violation. Technique A is therefore deliberately scoped to the gate's OWN implementing types (`AesGcmEncryptionService`/`RsaSignatureService`/`EcdsaSignatureService`'s own constructor and gated-member IL), never a repository-wide "no production code calls a sync member" scan — the latter shape would flag `07.Messaging`'s legitimate call site; the chosen shape structurally cannot, because it never inspects call sites outside the three gate-implementing types.
2. `06.Persistence` established that `EncryptionKeyProviderCapabilities.IsGenuinelySynchronous` is a static provider-identity check `CachedEncryptionKeyProvider` can never satisfy for a KMS inner provider, and designed `PreWarmedEncryptionKeyProvider` (P-498) to "honestly earn" `ISynchronousEncryptionKeyProvider` by never touching its wrapped inner provider synchronously. This suggests a generalized, platform-wide "no type claiming `ISynchronousEncryptionKeyProvider`/`ISynchronousAsymmetricKeyProvider` may contain a blocking-bridge call (`.GetAwaiter().GetResult()`/`.Result`/`.Wait()`) anywhere in its own method bodies" guard would be a MORE durable lock than this phase's own narrower gate-reachability check — it would catch ANY future marker-claiming implementer cheating the contract, not just the two types this phase targets. EVALUATED AND DELIBERATELY DEFERRED, not implemented here: `06.Persistence`'s own T-142/T-143 already behaviorally prove the one shipped example (call-counting test doubles against `PreWarmedEncryptionKeyProvider`'s real warm/miss paths) more precisely than a generic IL scan could, and P-504's own dispatched acceptance criteria do not ask for it — inventing new WO scope beyond what was dispatched is not this planning pass's call to make. Recorded as a candidate follow-up phase for a future work order.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (production — one new method), `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` (test project).
- New files: none — both techniques extend existing files.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/CryptoIsolationRules.cs` (Technique B — new method); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SecureDefaultsAssertionTests.cs` (Technique A — new contrived fixtures now, real-assembly GATING tests once `01.Core`'s P-492/P-493 ship past Design into Core); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/CryptoIsolationRulesTests.cs` (or wherever this project's existing `CryptoIsolationRules` tests live — Technique B's two real-assembly tests, immediate); `SharedKernel.Cryptography.csproj` (Technique B's T-365 — a TEMPORARY `PackageReference` mutation, added and reverted within the same session, never committed); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (already applied by this planning pass); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. Technique A reuses two EXISTING `SecureDefaultsAssertion` methods unchanged (zero new production code — the third phase in this family to do so, after `SK.00.CorrelationIdValidationGuard` and `SK.00.CacheEncryptionAndRedisValidationLock`'s Technique B). Technique B is a new `ConditionList`-returning method, not a source-level anti-pattern a Roslyn analyzer should catch — following the established "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention of every phase in this family. SK0037 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID, not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. Technique A reuses `SecureDefaultsAssertion.AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type calleeDeclaringType, string calleeMethodName)` (WO-061/P-401) and `.AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType(Type declaringType, string methodName, Type expectedExceptionType)` (WO-062/P-410) UNCHANGED — no new Mono.Cecil technique, no new method on `SecureDefaultsAssertion`, no new SK ID.
2. Technique A's targets (CONFIRM against real shipped source before writing the real-assembly test, per this domain's standing "never assume, confirm against real source" discipline — do not trust these names as final): `AesGcmEncryptionService`'s constructor (`.ctor`) is expected to invoke `EncryptionKeyProviderCapabilities.IsGenuinelySynchronous`, per D-70's own "computed once at construction time, cached as a private field" design; each of `Encrypt`/`Decrypt`/`EncryptToString`/`DecryptToString` is expected to construct-and-throw `System.NotSupportedException`. `RsaSignatureService`/`EcdsaSignatureService`'s constructors are expected to invoke `AsymmetricKeyProviderCapabilities.IsGenuinelySynchronous` the same way, per D-73's "exactly per P-492's pattern"; `Sign`/`Verify` are each expected to construct-and-throw `System.NotSupportedException`.
3. Technique A is DELIBERATELY SCOPED to the gate's OWN implementing types' own method bodies — never a repository-wide "no production code calls a sync `ISymmetricEncryptionService`/`IAsymmetricSignatureService` member" scan. See Goal's Input 1 for why: `07.Messaging`'s payload-transform serializers have a structurally-unavoidable, legitimate sync call site (proven by reflection against the installed MassTransit assembly — no async overload exists anywhere on its serializer interfaces) that a call-site-presence scan would incorrectly flag. The chosen technique only inspects `AesGcmEncryptionService`/`RsaSignatureService`/`EcdsaSignatureService`'s own IL and therefore cannot reach `07.Messaging`'s call site at all.
4. `AssertMethodBodyInvokesMethod`'s/`AssertMethodBodyThrowsExceptionType`'s existing closure-method-scanning extension (proven necessary by T-318, reused unchanged by every subsequent application) already covers the case where either the capability-check invocation or the exception construction is hosted inside a compiler-generated closure rather than the constructor's/member's own direct IL body — confirm this against the real shipped shape rather than assume it, per Rule 2.
5. Technique B is a NEW method, `CryptoIsolationRules.CryptographyCoreHasNoThirdPartyDependencies(Assembly cryptographyAssembly) → ConditionList`, mirroring `RedisTopologyRules.CachingAbstractionsHasNoInfrastructureDependencies`'s exact multi-term `Types.InAssembly(...).Should().NotHaveDependencyOn(term)` shape. Forbidden terms: `"Konscious"` (P-495's future Argon2 dependency — the phase's literal WO-081 target) and, as an ADDITIVE re-check using the identical mechanism, `"Azure.Security.KeyVault"`/`"Azure.Identity"` (P-447's already-shipped KeyVault.Azure dependency, previously verified ONLY via `01.Core`'s own `.nuspec`-inspection technique in `SharedKernel.Consumer.Tests` — a different project, a different technique, outside this domain's own jurisdiction until now).

Technique B's regression proof (T-365, satisfying WO-081/P-504's own second acceptance criterion literally) is a TEMPORARY mutation, never a committed change: add `<PackageReference Include="Konscious.Security.Cryptography.Argon2" Version="..."/>` directly to `SharedKernel.Cryptography.csproj`, rebuild, confirm `CryptographyCoreHasNoThirdPartyDependencies` genuinely fails against the mutated assembly, then revert the `.csproj` fully before commit (`git diff` must confirm empty) — mirroring this family's now-standard "temporary sanity check, confirmed to fail, then reverted" verification technique, applied here to a real `PackageReference` mutation rather than a deliberately-wrong assertion expectation.
8. No new SK diagnostic ID for either technique — both are real-assembly regression-lock checks on a design/dependency-confinement invariant, not source-level anti-patterns a Roslyn analyzer should catch, following the established convention of every phase in this family. SK0037 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID.
9. The generalized "marker-honesty" guard considered in Goal's Input 2 is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this phase — do not add it as an unrequested extension. If a future work order dispatches it, it belongs as its own phase in this same family, not folded into this one's task rows after the fact.

## Phase SK.00.CoreDiRegistrationConventionLock — Governance: Mechanically Lock the 01.Core TryAdd/TryAddEnumerable DI-Registration Convention <!-- phase-key: SK.00.CoreDiRegistrationConventionLock -->

### Goal

Root `state-map.md` P-523 (WO-083, depends on P-518) asks for an architecture-test/analyzer rule verifying every DI extension method in `01.Core` uses `TryAdd*`/`TryAddEnumerable` rather than plain `Add*` for its own service registrations — closing the door on P-518's corrected convention (fixing the confirmed `AddSharedKernelCryptography()` double-registration bug and the "first registration should win" override-semantics inversion) silently drifting back the next time someone adds a registration line. P-523 arrived with no domain-level design of its own — this phase supplies it, mirroring this platform's established "follow a corrected default with a structural lock" pattern (P-401, P-410, P-432, P-489, P-490).

Confirmed on disk before this phase's implementation session: `01.Core`'s P-518 (WO-083) had already shipped — every one of `01.Core`'s nine DI extension classes across nine packages (`SharedKernel.Primitives`, `SharedKernel.Configuration`, `SharedKernel.Compression`, `SharedKernel.Cryptography`, `SharedKernel.Cryptography.Argon2`, `SharedKernel.Cryptography.KeyVault.Azure`, `SharedKernel.FeatureManagement`, `SharedKernel.Localization`, `SharedKernel.Validation`) already used `TryAddSingleton`/`TryAddEnumerable` exclusively for its own registrations, confirmed by direct grep across every production (non-`.Tests`) `.cs` file in `01.Core` — zero plain `services.AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`AddTransient` call sites remained outside test fixtures, doc-comment `<code>` samples (never compiled, and explicitly the consumer's own registration recipe for `IClock`/`IIdGenerator`, which deliberately ship no package-owned DI extension), and `SharedKernel.FeatureManagement`'s deliberately-untouched third-party `Microsoft.FeatureManagement.AddFeatureManagement(...)` call. Real-assembly wiring is therefore IMPLEMENTED as a GATING test immediately, not deferred as a Cross-Domain Dependency.

**A correction to the phase's own naive first reading, caught before any code was written.** Root P-523's own "What is needed" prose could be misread as "every DI registration in `01.Core` must use `TryAdd*`" without qualification — but `01.Core`'s own P-518 design record (see root `state-map.md`'s 2026-09-09 changelog entries) documents two DELIBERATE `TryAddEnumerable` registrations that a naive "no plain `Add*`" OR "always `TryAddSingleton`" rule would get wrong in different directions: `SharedKernel.Validation.AddNationalIdValidator<TValidator>()` (resolved via `sp.GetServices<INationalIdValidator>()` — a `TryAddSingleton` there would silently drop every country validator after the first) and `SharedKernel.Cryptography.KeyVault.Azure`'s `IValidateOptions<AzureKeyVaultCryptographyOptions>` registration (which coexists with the BCL's own `DataAnnotationValidateOptions<T>` registered by the preceding `AddValidatedOptions` call against the same service type — a `TryAddSingleton` there silently dropped the custom cross-field validator, a real regression P-518's own implementation session caught and fixed). The rule this phase builds therefore asserts absence of the FORBIDDEN VERBS (`AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`AddTransient`) specifically — never presence of any one particular verb — so `TryAddEnumerable` (and any future legitimately-`TryAddSingleton`-registered service) both pass without needing a per-service-type exception list. Verified directly by reading the real, shipped `AddNationalIdValidator`/`AzureKeyVaultCryptographyOptionsValidator` registration source before writing the predicate, not assumed from the changelog description alone.

**A second thing verified rather than assumed:** whether `SharedKernel.FeatureManagement`'s untouched third-party `AddFeatureManagement(...)` call would need an explicit predicate exemption. It does not — `MsftFeatureManagement.ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddFeatureManagement` is a different method NAME (`"AddFeatureManagement"`, not `"AddSingleton"`/`"AddScoped"`/`"AddTransient"`) on a different DECLARING TYPE than the BCL's `ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions`, so the predicate's name+declaring-type match structurally cannot reach it — no exemption list of any kind was needed anywhere in this rule.

### Scope

- Package(s) affected: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests` (production — one new predicate, one new rules class), `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests` (test project — one new test file, nine new test-only `ProjectReference`s).
- New files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoPlainServiceCollectionRegistrationPredicate.cs`; `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/CoreArchitectureRules.cs` (the platform's first `01.Core`-domain architecture-rule class); `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/CoreArchitectureRulesTests.cs`.
- Modified files: `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` (eight new `ProjectReference`s — `SharedKernel.Primitives`/`.Configuration`/`.Compression`/`.FeatureManagement`/`.Localization`/`.Validation`/`.Cryptography.Argon2`/`.Cryptography.KeyVault.Azure`; `SharedKernel.Cryptography` was already referenced); `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` (new `CoreArchitectureRules` entry, this phase's Changelog entry); `00.Governance/state-map.md` (this phase).
- Deleted files: none.

### Diagnostic Registry Changes (analyzers only)

None. This is a `ConditionList`-returning NetArchTest rule (an architecture test, not a source-level anti-pattern), following the established "boundary/regression rule, no ID" convention shared by `RedisTopologyRules`/`EfCorePackageHygieneRules`/`SecurityArchitectureRules`. SK0037 remains the next available sequential Roslyn-analyzer ID, not consumed here.

### Implementation Rules

1. New Mono.Cecil technique on `NoPlainServiceCollectionRegistrationPredicate : ICustomRule`: for every method body declared on a scanned type, flag a `Call`/`Callvirt` instruction whose resolved `MethodReference.Name` is `"AddSingleton"`, `"AddScoped"`, or `"AddTransient"` AND whose `MethodReference.DeclaringType.FullName` equals `"Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions"` (confirmed via direct reflection against the platform's pinned `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`/`.Abstractions` `10.0.11`, not assumed).
2. Name-only matching would already be unambiguous — no BCL overload of `TryAddSingleton`/`TryAddScoped`/`TryAddTransient`/`TryAddEnumerable` (declared on the DIFFERENT type `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions.ServiceCollectionDescriptorExtensions`) shares a name with the forbidden `Add*` family. The declaring-type check is added anyway for defense-in-depth (near-zero extra cost, forecloses a hypothetical unrelated same-named method in a future `01.Core` package) — mirroring, not duplicating, `NoSecurityContextSingletonRegistrationPredicate`'s own precedent of documenting exactly this kind of matching-precision tradeoff.
3. No exemption list of any kind — verified unnecessary per Goal's two verification notes above (`TryAddEnumerable` already passes structurally since it is not in the forbidden name set; `AddFeatureManagement` already fails to match on both name and declaring type).
4. `CoreArchitectureRules.DiExtensionsUseTryAddRegistrationConvention(params Assembly[] assemblies) → ConditionList` follows the exact `Types.InAssemblies(assemblies).That().HaveNameStartingWith(string.Empty).Should().MeetCustomRule(...)` shape `SecurityArchitectureRules.NoSingletonRegistrationOfSecurityContextTypes` established — scans every type in the supplied assemblies, not merely the known DI extension classes, since direct grep confirmed no other `01.Core` production code touches `IServiceCollection` at all.
5. Scoped to `01.Core` for this phase only, per P-523's own acceptance criteria — the caller supplies exactly the nine `01.Core` assemblies; nothing about the predicate itself is `01.Core`-specific, so extending it to another domain's own DI extension methods in a future work order is a drop-in reuse, not a redesign.
6. Non-vacuous verification deliberately never edits any `01.Core` file, even temporarily (per this session's explicit "do not edit `01.Core`" instruction) — two techniques substitute for this family's usual "temporarily wrong expectation, confirmed to fail, then reverted" proof, which does not apply here since this is an absence check with no expected-value argument to perturb: (a) three contrived fixtures (one per forbidden verb) compiled through the exact same predicate class prove it genuinely fires; (b) the real, compiled `SharedKernel.Cryptography.dll`'s `AddSharedKernelCryptography` method body was inspected read-only via a standalone Mono.Cecil script (against the build output, never the source) and confirmed to contain nine genuine `TryAddSingleton`/`TryAddKeyedSingleton` calls — proving the real-assembly pass-path test (T-372) scans substantial real IL, not an empty method body.

### File-Level Plan

|------|---------|--------|---------|
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Predicates/NoPlainServiceCollectionRegistrationPredicate.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | The name+declaring-type IL detection technique |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests/Rules/CoreArchitectureRules.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests | Create | `DiExtensionsUseTryAddRegistrationConvention(params Assembly[])` — the platform's first `01.Core`-domain rules class |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests/CoreArchitectureRulesTests.cs` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Create | T-366–T-372 |
| `SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests.csproj` | SharedKernel.ArchitectureTests.Tests | Modify | Eight new test-only `ProjectReference`s (`PrivateAssets="all"`) for T-372's real-assembly scan |
| `00.Governance/CLAUDE.md` | — | Modify | `CoreArchitectureRules` entry, Changelog |

Real-assembly wiring is therefore IMPLEMENTED (T-372), not deferred as a Cross-Domain Dependency.
- Unblocks: nothing structurally — a terminal, self-contained regression-prevention rule, mirroring every prior phase in this family's own "close it before it drifts again" motivation, applied here to `01.Core`'s corrected DI-registration idiom specifically.

## Phase SK.00.ServiceDefaultsSplitRepoint — Governance: Re-point the ServiceDefaults Layering Rules at the Split Packages <!-- phase-key: SK.00.ServiceDefaultsSplitRepoint -->

### Goal

WO-084 (root P-531–P-537) split `13.ServiceDefaults`' composition package into a base that references no other SharedKernel package plus thirteen `SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults.*` integration packages. The workflow and scheduler readiness checks — and with them the WO-047 `13→17` and P-466 `13→19` layering grants — moved into `SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults.Workflows.Temporal` and `SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults.Scheduling`; mutual-TLS composition moved into `SharedKernel.ServiceDefaults.Security.Mtls`. This phase (root P-535) makes the three real-assembly governance tests inspect the packages that now hold those types.

`ServiceDefaultsWorkflowLayeringRules` and `ServiceDefaultsSchedulingLayeringRules` were already parameterized by `Assembly`, and their real-assembly tests resolve it through `typeof(...)`, so no rule changed — the tests follow the moved types once the project references them. **The risk this phase closes is vacuity, not breakage.** Each rule reports success for any assembly that never touches the granted package, so a test left pointing at the base — which after WO-084 references no SharedKernel package at all — would pass while inspecting nothing.

## Phase SK.00.DomainFactoryAndValueObjectValidationGuard — Governance: Enforce `IAggregateFactory` and `EnsureValid` <!-- phase-key: SK.00.DomainFactoryAndValueObjectValidationGuard -->

### Goal

Root P-542, raised by `03.Domain` P-540. The user kept `IAggregateFactory` on condition that it gets a real job, and P-540's explicit value-object validation left one trap: a value object that forgets `EnsureValid()` compiles and is silently never validated. Give the marker a rule and close the trap statically.

**Decisions.** The factory rule takes open generic anchors from the caller (`typeof(IAggregateFactory<,>)`, `typeof(ValidationResult<>)`), like every other domain rule, so the package still needs no `SharedKernel.Domain` reference; a closed or wrong-arity anchor throws instead of passing vacuously (new `RuleAnchor.GenericDefinition`). "Lives in a domain assembly" is expressed by applying the rule to each domain assembly, not by guessing assembly roles. SK0037 resolves `SharedKernel.Domain.ValueObjects.ValueObject` by fully qualified name through the semantic model, exempts `SingleValueObject<TValue>` (which calls `EnsureValid()` itself), abstract classes, and a `Validate()` that declares no rules (`[]`, `null`, `default`, `Array/Enumerable.Empty`, `yield break`), which keeps `Money` and similar guard-validated types quiet without suppressions.
